title: China Resources launches tender for 500 MW Yangjiang offshore wind project
content:
China Resources Group's Shouzheng Electronic Bidding Platform has released
a tender for wind turbine foundation and installation works at the Yangjiang
Sanshan Island Four Offshore Wind Farm
project.
The 500 MW project is located in the southern sea area of Hailing Island,
Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province.
According to the tender announcement, the scope of work includes the procurement,
transportation, foundation construction and installation of 25 wind turbines,
each with a capacity of 20 MW.
Bidders will be responsible for all work related to the construction of
the turbine foundations, installation and foundation safety monitoring.
The tender also includes navigation safety assurance measures during the
construction period, as well as the installation and management of temporary
navigation aids and support facilities.
Companies bidding for the installation package are required to develop
an offshore installation plan based on their vessel capabilities and construction
experience. The plan must include detailed analysis and calculations.
The successful bidder will install electrical cabinets, lay power and fibre
optic cables, perform fibre optic splicing, completing associated cable
and secondary wiring works within the offshore converter station scope.
Additional tender responsibilities include surveying, testing, logistics
support, communications, environmental protection, equipment storage and
transport.
Project completion is currently scheduled for 31 July 2028.

title: East Anglia THREE reaches foundation installation milestone
content:
ScottishPower Renewables and Masdar have successfully installed 95 monopile
foundations at the 1.4 GW East
Anglia THREE offshore wind farm.
The foundations were installed using Seaway 7's jack-up vessel, Seaway
Ventus. The partnership will continue as Seaway 7 supports the inter-array
cable installation process for the East Anglia THREE wind farm.
The monopiles weighed around 1,200 to 1,800 tonnes and stand 67 to 84 metres
high, with diameters of 10.6 metres. These measurements make them the largest
monopiles to be installed from a jack-up vessel in Europe.
Additionally, 95 transition pieces have been also been installed at the
wind farm.
Charlie Jordan, CEO of ScottishPower Renewables, said: "East Anglia
THREE is our biggest wind farm ever, and the completion of the foundation
installation is a true engineering triumph."
The company outlined the next stages of the project, commenting: "And
there's more to come as the installation of the 95 turbines, with huge
115 metre blades, the biggest built and used here in the U.K., crosses
the halfway mark and we move ever closer to bringing the wind farm's 1.4
GW of clean energy to life."
Highlighting the significance of the project, the company said that once
completed, East Anglia THREE will provide clean energy for 1.3 million
U.K. homes, helping strengthen energy security while meeting growing energy
Construction of the wind farm will continue in the coming months, with
the project expected to become fully operational by the end of 2026.

title: Siemens successfully installs lightweight integrated offshore substation
content:
Siemens Energy has announced the successful installation of its first lightweight
integrated offshore substation at the Yuetuo
Island Offshore Wind Farm.
This installation marks the first deployment of the company’s High-Voltage
Unit (HV-TSU) concept.
The company stated that, by integrating high-voltage components into a
smaller and lighter design, it reduces topside weight while ensuring reliability.
This innovative design will help optimise project execution, reduce complexity,
and support new offshore wind developments.
Siemens aims for the successful application of this technology to support
new grid developments, helping to boost renewable energy generation.

title: Stillstrom successfully demonstrates automated offshore charging system
content:
Stillstrom by Maersk has announced the successful completion of a milestone
trial, demonstrating that offshore vessel charging can be fully automated.
The trial was carried out in partnership with offshore wind vessel operator
ESVAGT and Semco Maritime, which hosted the test at its yard in Esbjerg,
Denmark.
Kristian Borum Jørgensen, CEO of Stillstrom, said: “Cable control is one
of the trickier parts of offshore charging to get right, and this successful
trial showed our system safely managing it automatically as the vessel
moves, and communicating reliably well beyond our planned range.”
During the trial, a charging connector was deployed to a vessel from a
height of 15.5 metres, representative of the height at which a Stillstrom
charging system could be installed on an offshore wind turbine or substation.
A tower mounted cable reel held 125 metres of cable.
Traditionally, connecting a vessel to an offshore power source while it
maintains dynamic positioning (DP) requires careful management of a moving
cable, a task that has typically required manual oversight.
The trial of the Stillstrom Offshore eCharger (SOeC) demonstrated that
this cable management process can be performed automatically, potentially
reducing both operational costs and safety risks.
The trial was witnessed by DNV as part of its technology qualification
process.

title: The Rudong offshore wind project has officially transmitted 10 billion kWh
content:
China Three Gorges Corporation said its 800 MW Rudong offshore wind project
in Jiangsu Province has transmitted more than 10 billion kWh of electricity
since entering operation.
The project, which has been operating at full capacity since 2021, is the
first offshore wind farm in Asia to use flexible direct current (DC) transmission
technology.
According to the company, it is also the world's largest offshore wind
power project using flexible DC transmission in terms of both installed
capacity and voltage level.
China Three Gorges Corporation said the wind farm generates enough electricity
to supply about 4 million households annually. The company added that the
use of flexible DC transmission has reduced transmission line losses by
around 1.2 percentage points compared with conventional alternating current
(AC) transmission and delivered cumulative transmission cost savings of
more than 735 million yuan.

title: KBR to provide pre-FEED for Moroccan renewable ammonia project
content:
KBR to provide pre-FEED for Moroccan renewable ammonia project
560,000 tons per year, 900 MW electrolyser capacity
KBR has been selected by ORNX Green Hydrogen for pre-FEED work on a renewable ammonia project in southern Morocco. Supported through funding from the U.S. Trade and Development Agency, the production project has a planned capacity of 560,000 tons per year of ammonia, featuring renewable energy generation and 900 MW of installed electrolysers. The project is also one of the first successful recipients of the “Morocco Offer”, a scheme launched in 2022 to support the development of renewable hydrogen & derivatives production projects.
At launch the ORNX consortium included Ortus from the USA, Acciona from Spain, and Nordex from Germany. The new announcement indicates not only the involvement of KBR, but also notable ammonia energy players GE Vernova, Electric Hydrogen and Terabase. ORNX’s project aims to help “establish a large-scale, export-oriented supply of low-carbon ammonia for global markets”, noting demand for low-carbon ammonia in fertilizer, marine & industrial fuel sectors is also on the rise.
KBR is proud to support ORNX and USTDA on this important low cost ammonia initiative in Morocco. As a global leader in ammonia technology, KBR is uniquely positioned to help developers accelerate project maturity, optimize plant performance and reduce execution risk. This award reflects the strength of our integrated approach and our commitment to enabling the energy transition through scalable, commercially viable solutions.
Jay Ibrahim, President Sustainable Technology Solutions at KBR, in his organisation’s official press release, 12 Aug 2026
We are very grateful to KBR for its considerable support in working with USTDA to reach this important milestone for our ammonia project in Laayoune. This funding will ensure the successful completion of the pre-FEED studies lead by world-renowned KBR, together with a consortium which includes GE Vernova, Electric Hydrogen and Terabase. We look forward to working closely with our partners as we accelerate towards the FEED and Final Investment Decision for our project.
Peter Gish, President and CEO of ORNX, in KBR’s official press release, 12 Aug 2026

title: 10 Best-Selling EVs in the US in the First Half of 2026
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Market Analysis
US EV sales fell 23.8% after the federal tax credit expired, yet these 10 models still accounted for 72% of all EVs sold.
August 17, 2026
10 Slides
Start slideshow
Tesla Model Y.
For most of the past decade, electric vehicle sales in the US grew every single year. Federal tax credits and state rebates fueled this consistent growth, leading automakers to build battery plants all across the country, like in Georgia, Tennessee, and Michigan. Everyone in the auto industry seemed to believe the $7,500 federal clean vehicle tax credit was a permanent fixture of the market.
That is, until Congress ended the tax credit on September 30, 2025. Buyers rushed to make their purchases in the third quarter of 2025 to beat the deadline, but the market still shrank as expected. For the first half of 2026,
Kelley Blue Book estimates
US EV sales fell to roughly 463,000 units, down 23.8% from the same period a year earlier. Sales in the second quarter alone fell 20.5% year over year.
Automakers responded by cutting prices instead of production. Several brands took $7,500 to $9,800 off their entire electric lineups in the months after the deadline, absorbing the lost credit themselves to keep sticker prices palatable for consumers. Others introduced cheaper entry trims with smaller battery packs, trading range for a sub-$40,000 MSRP.

title: US drone battery makers target China supply
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Battery Manufacturing
Amprius Technologies and Packet Digital are scaling domestic drone battery production to reduce Pentagon reliance on Chinese suppliers for UAS programs.
August 17, 2026
5 Min Read
A member of the US Army 7th Army Training Command pilots an ADM4 surveillance drone.
Sean Gallup/Getty Images
At a Glance
Amprius ships 450 Wh/kg silicon-anode cells from California pilot line to multiple drone customers
Packet Digital receives $9.8 million Navy contract to scale lithium-ion cell production in Fargo
Pentagon's Blue UAS fleet still uses Chinese batteries despite 2020 NDAA procurement restrictions
Over the last decade, the U.S. military has grown increasingly dependent on small unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for many operations. In a UAS, the battery is one of the most important components, determining crucial factors like the aircraft’s endurance, payload, and range. Only a few suppliers worldwide make cells sufficiently performant for UAS, and most of them are based in China.
To bolster national security, the U.S. government sought to limit China’s dominance in UAS battery supply through procurement regulations. In 2020, lawmakers passed the
National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)
to bar the Department of Defense from buying unmanned aircraft with Chinese flight controllers, radios, or cameras. Unfortunately, the NDAA did not cover components that neither store nor transmit data, such as motors, speed controllers, and batteries. This loophole, combined with China’s supply chain strength, contributed to
the Pentagon’s Blue UAS fleet still using Chinese batteries
Related:
Korean EVs Crush Tesla, German Rivals in Battery Longevity Test
Where regulators see limitations, domestic suppliers see opportunities to help solve this supply chain crisis. In this piece, we'll take a look at two battery suppliers in the U.S. that are ramping up production for the military’s drone program,
Amprius Technologies
Packet Digital
Drone batteries’ production challenges
Drones need batteries that are both lightweight and high-power to balance performance, range, and efficiency. Therefore, the ideal drone battery is the one that offers the most energy per unit weight.
In many cases, the primary constraint on a battery cell’s energy density is its anode material. While graphite is the industry-standard anode material for Li-ion batteries,
it has an energy density of only 372 mAh/g.
In contrast, silicon has an energy density of 3,579 mAh/g, meaning a silicon-based battery could theoretically offer 10x greater energy per unit weight.
The catch, however, is that silicon can swell up to 300% as it charges in a lithium-ion battery, which cracks particles and shortens cell life. To mitigate these risks, battery manufacturers can nanostructure the silicon and build void space into the particles, but that is difficult and costly to do at commercial scale.
Benefits of nanostructured silicon for lithium-ion battery anodes. Credit: Pavlovskii et al.
Anode chemistry is only half the reason many drone battery suppliers are located offshore. The other half is the fact that U.S. battery manufacturers don’t produce enough drone batteries to meet military demand. Instead, Chinese suppliers eclipse domestic ones in both volume and cost.
To onshore drone battery production, domestic manufacturers must either build batteries with much higher energy density or standard cells at higher volumes.
Related:
10 Best-Selling EVs in the US in the First Half of 2026
Amprius’ Fremont pilot line
Amprius Technologies is one of the first domestic suppliers to produce high-energy-density silicon batteries. In July 2025, the company
announced
that it had delivered its silicon-anode battery cells to multiple drone and UAS customers from its Fremont, California, pilot line.
According to the company, those shipments included 450 Wh/kg high-energy cells to AALTO, an Airbus subsidiary, along with balanced energy-and-power cells for tactical and commercial drone makers. Amprius says third-party testing has validated its batteries at 500 Wh/kg and 1,300 Wh/L.
Amprius ships high-performance silicon anode cells to multiple drone customers from its US pilot line. Credit: Amprius Technologies.
This level of energy density is significant for endurance UAS. For example, AALTO’s Zephyr is a solar-powered solution, meaning it needs to store enough energy during the day to fly through the night. According to Pierre-Antoine Aubourg, chief technology officer at AALTO, “[Amprius’] silicon anode technology has already enabled Zephyr to operate in the stratosphere overnight for months at a time.”
Despite all this promising news, Amprius can’t replace Chinese battery suppliers because it still can’t produce at scale. At the moment, Amprius’ Fremont facility is primarily an R&D hub, with the company planning to contract out cell manufacturing abroad. So far, the company claims to have already secured more than 1.8 GWh of production capacity, including an agreement in South Korea. Therefore, the Pentagon will have to wait if it wants fully domestically-made batteries for its entire UAS program.
Related:
GM Exits Samsung SDI Battery Venture as Ohio Ultium Plant Restarts Production
Packet Digital’s Navy cell plant
Whereas Amprius was targeting high energy density, Packet Digital is targeting high capacity cell production.
In May, Packet Digital and its subsidiary Badland Batteries
announced
that the U.S. Navy had awarded them $9.8 million to enter Phase 3 of their contract under the Logistics UAS Family of Advanced Batteries program. Badland previously started commissioning its Fargo, North Dakota factory, so Phase 3 will cover production scaling and supply chain validation as it ramps up throughput to meet Navy requirements.
In addition to building out manufacturing capacity for NDAA-compliant cells, Badland says it will use the Phase 3 funds to support multiple lithium-ion chemistries to meet changing Navy requirements. According to Terri Zimmerman, CEO of Packet Digital, “Phase 3 is where years of planning, engineering and investment turn into high-rate production capability for the U.S. Navy, national defense and commercial markets.”
The U.S. Navy contract also brings political benefits. U.S. Sen. John Hoeven said the funding “keeps that work moving forward in North Dakota, supports good-paying manufacturing jobs and helps ensure a secure supply chain while reducing our reliance on materials from adversaries.” Because Phase 3 has just begun, it’s worth noting that no one knows whether Badland will successfully produce UAS cells at volumes high enough to replace Chinese manufacturers.
Two routes to the same capability
The announcements showcase two companies contributing to a domestic drone battery supply chain. Amprius sits at one end, aiming for energy densities that outcompete imported cells, and Packet Digital sits at the other, building manufacturing capacity that rivals offshore suppliers.
While there is hope for domestic cell production, throughput has yet to be proven. With the NDAA and other laws still permitting the U.S. military to import batteries from China, the future of domestic drone batteries may hinge on whether they can be competitive on a cost-per-watt-hour basis.

title: APAC Data Center Pipeline Surges as Pre-Leasing Tightens Supply
content:
Asia-Pacific’s data center development pipeline reached a record 26.5 GW in the first half of 2026 as investment in AI and cloud infrastructure accelerated across the region, according to a new report from Cushman & Wakefield.
The milestone comes as colocation vacancy rates continue to decline, highlighting the region’s urgent need for additional capacity to meet growing demand.
The data center capacity pipeline grew by 7.1 GW during the six-month period, one of the strongest half-year increases on record. Of the 26.5 GW total, approximately 4.8 GW was under construction, and 21.7 GW remained in the planning stage.
According to
Cushman & Wakefield, the region also brought about 1.4 GW of new operational capacity online. Despite those deliveries, colocation vacancy rates declined from 10.9% in the second half of 2025 to 10.3%, indicating that customer demand continued to absorb new supply.
Cushman’s report covers Australia, mainland China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.
Related:
Galaxy Bets Its Data Center Edge on Power, Not ‘Bragawatts’
“New supply is being absorbed quickly, with a growing share of capacity pre-leased before delivery, meaning much of the new stock is already committed when it becomes operational,” Pritesh Swamy, head of research and consulting at Cushman & Wakefield’s Asia-Pacific data center group, told
Data Center Knowledge
“While conditions vary across markets, we expect this trend to continue as strong demand and limited new supply keep availability tight.”
Swamy added that power constraints, longer development timelines, and evolving technical requirements are prompting customers to commit to capacity well before project completion.
Southeast Asia Leads Construction, Seoul Squeezed
Southeast Asia accounted for approximately half of all capacity under construction in APAC, with 2.38 GW. Malaysia led the region with 1.04 GW under construction, followed by Thailand with 859 MW, with much of the expansion concentrated in Johor, Indonesia, and Bangkok.
Johor’s capacity under construction grew by 91% to 602 MW, while its overall development pipeline grew 28% to 3.09 GW. When existing and future capacity are combined, Johor exceeds 4 GW, making it the largest market in Cushman’s APAC maturity index.
Bangkok’s construction pipeline rose 148% to 859 MW, while its total development pipeline nearly doubled to 2.08 GW. Sydney’s pipeline increased 65% to 2.13 GW, Jakarta’s grew 56% to 1.70 GW, and Mumbai’s expanded 31% to 1.73 GW.
Related:
CoreWeave Enters APAC Data Center Race With Indonesia Expansion
Japan added 293 MW of operational capacity, lifting its total to 1.8 GW and moving it ahead of India as APAC’s second-largest operational market behind mainland China. Cushman projects that Australia, India, Japan, and Malaysia will each exceed 2 GW of operating capacity by 2028.
Greater Seoul recorded just 1.1% colocation vacancy rate in the first half of 2026. While operational capacity rose 10%, the pipeline remained nearly flat, in an exceptionally tight market.
Major Data Center Projects Underway in Asia-Pacific
The Asia-Pacific region is witnessing significant data center development, with major projects underway to meet the demands of AI and cloud infrastructure. Key projects underway include:
CoreWeave
is currently expanding its AI cloud platform with
three facilities in Indonesia
. The Greater Jakarta deployment totals 360 MW of contracted IT power and is expected to come online in 2028, serving AI labs, startups, enterprises, and government customers across Southeast Asia.
In July,
Digital Edge
acquired land in South Korea to
develop 60 MW of AI-ready data capacity
, supported by a 90 MVA power agreement. The site will feature dual-feed power architecture supported by two independent 154 kV substations.
In June,
Gorilla Technology Group
announced plans for a
200 MW AI data center campus
in Korat, Thailand, with six data halls supporting 150 MW of IT load and approximately 76,000 GPUs at full deployment.
Also in June,
CDC Data Centres
in Australia secured a record 555 MW contract with an unnamed U.S. customer, with
capacity scheduled to enter operation
across new campuses in fiscal 2028 and 2029.
Related:
Do We Really Need Mega Next-Gen Data Center Campuses?
Planned Capacity Faces Challenges in Power Availability
The composition of the pipeline is as important as its size. Roughly 82% remains planned rather than under construction, leaving delivery dependent on power connections, land, permitting, financing and equipment availability.
Cushman concludes that APAC has entered a period of “power-constrained execution.”
While data centers historically clustered around network connectivity, AI infrastructure requires far greater electrical capacity and higher-density cooling. Development is shifting from saturated hubs toward peripheral districts and entirely new markets capable of supplying power at scale.
However, the shift does not mean established hubs are losing demand: Tokyo had just 4.4% vacancy and Singapore 4.8% in the first half of the year. Nevertheless, land and power constraints are limiting conventional expansion.
“Tight availability is likely to support rental growth and encourage further development, although rental data varies by market,” Swamy said. “More importantly, power and land constraints are increasingly influencing where new capacity can be built.”
This is encouraging developers and hyperscalers to look beyond established hubs toward secondary markets that can offer scalable power, land and connectivity.

title: PJM’s New Deal for Data Centers: Bring Power or Face Cuts
content:
PJM Interconnection
(PJM) has asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to create a conditional reliability framework for major new electricity users, including data centers. Filed on August 13, the proposal would allow big new facilities to enter service before sufficient new capacity is available to support their demand. In return, any portion of demand not backed by qualifying new capacity could be curtailed before other pre-emergency demand-response measures.
PJM defines a
“New Large Load”
as a large load that enters service or adds incremental demand after June 1, 2027. A Large Load is end-use customer demand with a cumulative peak of at least 50 MW at a single electrical site. Affiliated facilities within a one-mile radius can be treated as a single electrical site under the proposed rules.
New Loads Face Earlier Cuts
Under the proposal, load-serving entities (LSEs) serving New Large Loads must designate qualifying new capacity equal to or greater than the load’s peak demand. New Large Loads (50 MW or more) are not automatically subject to Interim Resource Adequacy Service (IRAS). Only the portion of demand not covered by qualifying new capacity would be subject to reductions during specified reliability conditions, and only before PJM calls for Pre-Emergency Load Management Response. A load with enough qualifying capacity to cover its registered peak would not face IRAS.
Related:
PJM Issued First Backup-Generator Warnings During Heat Wave
PJM says the arrangement preserves state authority over retail load-reduction programs. LSEs serving eligible loads would receive PJM’s reduction directive, while applicable distributors and state authorities would determine how the reduction is implemented. The filing leaves implementation details to
state-regulated retail arrangements
, including how a distributor would require, measure, and compensate a load reduction. PJM has said compensation for directed reductions would be subject to a FERC-approved rate and state jurisdiction.
PJM has requested an Oct. 12, 2026, effective date for the tariff revisions.
BYONC Provides a Path Out of IRAS
New Large Loads could reduce or eliminate their IRAS exposure through
Bring Your Own New Capacity (BYONC)
. Qualifying resources can include new generation, certain generation uprates, surplus interconnection service, certain repowered resources, fuel conversions, and storage. Certain demand resources and distributed energy resource aggregations can also qualify. Allocated Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP) Unforced Capacity (UCAP) could cover some or all of a New Large Load’s capacity requirement, reducing its IRAS exposure.
Related:
PJM Monitor: AI Data Center Growth Reshaping Power Markets
A load could use a combination of BYONC, RBP UCAP, and IRAS to cover any remaining requirement.
RPM Won’t Count Unsupported Load
PJM also proposes to change how certain New Large Loads affect its capacity auctions under the Reliability Pricing Model (RPM). Beginning with the 2029/30 delivery year, excluded New Large Load amounts would be reflected in PJM’s Variable Resource Requirement (VRR) curves used to determine capacity procurement. The proposed RTO curve would subtract the excluded New Large Load from the PJM Region Reliability Requirement.
In practical terms, PJM would not procure additional RPM capacity for incremental New Large Loads excluded under the proposed rules. Those loads would be responsible for securing their own qualifying capacity rather than adding that demand to what PJM procures in RPM.
The Registry Becomes a FERC Dispute
PJM would establish a Large Load Registry to support IRAS and other large-load programs. Schedule 11 would require information including a load’s location, peak demand, ramp schedule, telemetry specifications, BYONC, RBP UCAP, backup generation, and contracts or service agreements with its LSE.
The Independent Market Monitor (IMM), Monitoring Analytics, has challenged whether the proposed tariff requires enough evidence behind those entries.
Related:
White House Warns PJM to Reform Grid Governance ‘Before It Is Too Late’
Joseph Bowring, the Market Monitor’s executive director, told
Data Center Knowledge
that the tariff does not require data centers themselves to provide supporting evidence for the information submitted about their loads. He also wants a specific validation schedule. PJM’s proposal says it would update the registry “periodically,” while separately requiring parties to promptly report changes.
Bowring said the tariff should require ongoing validation, supporting evidence, and updates at least monthly or whenever a load’s status changes.
The tariff also says registry information “may be available” to state commissions, transmission owners, electric distributors, LSEs, the IMM, and FERC. Bowring said the Market Monitor should have explicit access rather than being included in a list of institutions that may receive the information.
PJM’s filing includes telemetry specifications as part of the registry data. The issue is also relevant to how data centers respond to grid disturbances, as seen when more than 3 GW of Northern Virginia data center load
transferred to backup power after a transmission-line fault
. Bowring said PJM should make clear whether covered loads will provide real-time telemetry, including customers taking less-than-full transmission service.
PJM spokesman Jeffrey Shields told
Data Center Knowledge
that PJM has enhanced its large-load vetting. Bowring disputed that assessment. “We have not seen any evidence of that,” he said.
Shields said utilities now provide PJM with additional information, including contract status, to establish firm commitments. Only firm loads with an Electric Service Obligation (ESO) or Construction Commitment (CC) are counted for capacity-market purposes, he said. Later-year requests remain part of regional transmission planning but are categorized as non-firm for capacity-market purposes. Shields also said PJM is working to add state commission review and an independent third-party review of its data center forecast.
Persistence Analytics Group has separately pressed FERC for stronger requirements around the evidence supporting registry entries. “The field tells you the value,” said Neil Osnato, founder of Persistence Analytics Group. “Provenance tells you why you should believe the value.”
Parties Enter the Case
PJM’s proposal did not emerge from stakeholder consensus. None of the 11 IRAS concepts put to an advisory vote in June received the two-thirds support required for approval, although PJM’s Board directed the filing.
FERC docket
has since drawn a broad cross-section of participants:
The Independent Market Monitor on market-rule compliance and market-design concerns.
The Maryland Public Service Commission on Maryland ratepayer interests.
The Illinois Attorney General on consumer costs.
The New Jersey Division of Rate Counsel on New Jersey ratepayer interests.
The PJM Industrial Customer Coalition representing large commercial, institutional, and industrial electricity users.
The PJM Power Providers Group on wholesale-market participants.
The Electric Power Supply Association (EPSA) on competitive power suppliers.
EDF Power Solutions on PJM project development.
Enchanted Rock on data centers and other high-load customers.
The motions to intervene do not establish substantive positions on PJM’s proposal.
In its July 2026 Board decision, PJM cited an expectation of roughly
70 GW of new large-load demand by 2038
, alongside approximately 15 GW of generation retirements since 2022.
FERC’s Combined Notice sets Sept. 3 at 5 p.m. ET as the deadline for comments and motions to intervene. IRAS exposure for eligible New Large Loads would begin June 1, 2027, while the VRR changes would begin with the 2029/30 delivery year.

title: Sunrun, Voltus Bring Home Batteries Into AI Capacity Push
content:
Sunrun will supply Voltus with capacity from residential solar-plus-storage systems in PJM and MISO grid operator regions under an agreement supporting Voltus’ “Bring Your Own Capacity” programs for AI hyperscale data centers, the companies said today (August 17).
Sunrun, a San Francisco-based provider of residential solar power and energy storage systems, did not disclose the capacity under the agreement, the number of participating homes, or the specific hyperscaler projects that will receive that capacity. The company said the resources will come from a portion of its thousands of residential storage-plus-solar systems in the two grid regions.
PJM is the largest grid operator in the US, covering parts of the Midwest and East Coast, and MISO (the Midcontinent Independent System Operator) manages the grid across much of the central US.
“Meeting growing energy demand requires us to maximize every single electron available across the country,” Sunrun CEO Mary Powell said in a statement. “In collaboration with Voltus, we are providing critical capacity from home batteries supported by funding from hyperscalers.”
Related:
Amazon Explores Grid Connection for 8,000-Acre AI Campus
Capacity Isn’t Deliverability
Voltus launched its BYOC program to enable large loads, such as hyperscalers, to bring firm, flexible capacity to support the grid and facilitate data center
interconnection
. The program aggregates distributed resources, such as batteries and smart thermostats, and pays participating homes and businesses for their resources.
The distinction between capacity and physical grid capability could limit what the arrangement does for individual data centers.
“Yes, distributed resources can enable speed-to-power as long as the state and federal market rules are aligned to enable it,” said Rob Gramlich, founder and president of Grid Strategies.
Gramlich said distributed resources can, in many cases, provide generation supply efficiently, while data centers increasingly are being required to bring their own generation. Transmission access is treated separately in regions with independent grid operators, he said.
“The important distinction is between installed battery nameplate and accredited capacity,” said Neil Osnato, founder of Persistence Analytics Group.
Residential batteries can be aggregated into a dispatchable resource, Osnato said, but their capacity value depends on the applicable market rules and how much dependable capacity the aggregation can commit and deliver.
A BYOC portfolio could help address a large load’s resource-adequacy requirement without resolving the physical constraint preventing that load from connecting, Osnato said.
Related:
PJM’s New Deal for Data Centers: Bring Power or Face Cuts
“If the purpose is purely to establish an aggregate capacity obligation at the market level, the geographic relationship may be broader,” he said. “But if someone is claiming that the VPP also relieves the infrastructure constraint preventing a specific data center from connecting, location becomes much more consequential.”
A battery located hundreds of miles from a data center could contribute to regional resource adequacy while doing little to address a local transformer, substation, transmission interface or voltage constraint serving the facility, he said.
Google Provides Precedent
June agreement with Google
provides a precedent for the model. Voltus said it would aggregate up to 100 MW of accredited distributed capacity annually in PJM for three years under a Google-funded virtual power plant. The resources can include batteries, smart thermostats and other flexible assets from homes and businesses.
The Sunrun agreement expands Voltus’ potential residential resource pool across PJM and MISO, but the companies did not say how much capacity will be added to Voltus’ programs.
Sunrun and Voltus also did not say whether the capacity announced Monday is already participating in PJM or MISO markets or will be newly enrolled for the hyperscaler programs.
Related:
Texas Orders Statewide Audit of AI Data Center Projects
Hyperscalers Become Buyers
The underlying VPP model is not new. What is changing is the potential role of hyperscalers as buyers of distributed capacity.
“The newer development is hyperscalers potentially treating distributed residential flexibility as part of their capacity procurement stack rather than as an incidental utility program,” Osnato said.
The model could give large electricity users another way to secure capacity as utilities and grid operators grapple with growing data center demand. But Osnato cautioned against treating distributed resources as a replacement for grid infrastructure.
“Capacity is not deliverability,” he said.
A distributed portfolio could defer or reduce certain infrastructure investments when its location and dispatch align with the relevant grid constraint, he said. But it cannot by itself eliminate inadequate transmission capability, insufficient substation or transformer capacity, voltage or stability limitations or other physical interconnection requirements.
Gramlich said New Jersey recently passed legislation intended to advance arrangements in which large loads bring their own generation, and that other states are considering similar approaches.
Sunrun separately announced in June that it, Renew Home and Tesla would work to deliver more than 16 GW of flexible energy capacity to hyperscalers and utilities. That initiative is separate from the Voltus agreement announced Monday.
The companies did not disclose the amount of capacity covered by the Sunrun-Voltus agreement, the number of participating homes or the specific hyperscaler projects that will receive the capacity.

title: CATL confirms Tener S for Quinbrook's massive Supernode Stage 3 in Australia - Energy Storage
content: In late July, global investment giant Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners made dual announcements about its massive Supernode battery , a planned 780 MW/3,074 MWh campus. The first was that the second of three stages had reached commercial operation in Southeast Queensland, with 250 MW/1,040 MWh online and operating, which brought the total capacity of the energy storage facility to 520 MW/1,858 MWh. It also announced that AUD 469 million (USD 327 million) debt financing had been secured for the 260 MW/1,216 MWh third stage, with the project backed by a 15-year offtake agreement with Queensland government-owned electricity generator Stanwell Corporation. Now, weeks later, Quinbrook’s technology partner and battery giant CATL has announced further details, saying it will supply Tener S systems for Stage 3 from its Tener series. CATL provided its EnerC Plus systems for Stages 1 and 2, all under a Long-Term Service Agreement (LTSA). Tener S is CATL’s newer BESS solution, as part of its Tener series. Tan Libin, CCO and co-president of sales and marketing at CATL, said “Energy storage is evolving from a standalone technology deployment into a strategic energy asset. The next stage of industry development will depend not only on technological advancement, but also on the ability to create long-term value through collaboration, innovation and scalable deployment. At CATL, we are committed to working with partners to unlock the full potential of energy storage assets and support the transition toward a more flexible and resilient energy system.” ESS News has contacted CATL for further confirmed information or a datasheet for the Tener S. It was first mentioned in regard to a supply to Grenergy in Spain earlier in 2026, and recent social media updates suggest each container hosts 6.017 MWh. EnerQB BESS mentioned, but not selected? Despite the use of the Tener S solution, CATL still mentioned, without update, its EnerQB BESS project , a specific eight-hour battery storage solution in pilot testing with Quinbrook, which was, at one time, being ‘considered for future stages’ of the Supernode development. When discussing the EnerQB BESS solution, Quinbrook’s CEO in Australia, Brian Restall, said the EnerQB BESS was much more energy-dense than existing technologies, adding that the advance is the result of design enhancements, even touting efficiency improvements, making mention of an evolution in parasitic load management which helped reduce temperatures, which may refer to cell balancing and/or auxiliary systems such as HVAC, pumps, controls, fans and other equipment. Battery cells can be balanced through passive or active cell-balancing systems, each requiring a different hardware approach. Passive balancing uses resistors to dissipate excess energy from higher-charged cells as heat. This creates an additional thermal load that must be managed within the battery system, whereas active balancing transfers energy between cells and can reduce energy losses and heat generation. title: SSE wins Irish planning consent to double BESS duration to 320 MWh - Energy Storage
content: Scottish-headquartered energy company SSE has secured planning consent from Mayo County Council for revised plans at its proposed 80 MW / 320 MWh Mullafarry battery energy storage system (BESS) near Killala, North Mayo, in Ireland, in the north-west. Located at Killala Business Park, the Mullafarry BESS is adjacent to SSE’s 104 MW Tawnaghmore Power Station. Originally, in an April 2025 approval, the project plan was for an 80 MW / 160 MWh, 38-unit battery storage facility. Following updated planning consent, the project has now been increased to up to 64 battery storage units and a four-hour duration system with the same peak power output. “We welcome Mayo County Council’s decision to approve our revised plans for the proposed Mullafarry battery energy storage system. This decision gives SSE the potential to significantly increase the energy output we can deliver through the project,” said Ghislain Demeuldre, head of onshore wind, solar and battery development at SSE Renewables. The approval means the project still requires a final investment decision by SSE, and if approved for investment, an estimated two-year construction phase would begin. “By storing electricity when supplies are high and making it available when needed, Mullafarry could help support a more secure, affordable and homegrown electricity system for Ireland. The project would also support jobs and local economic development during construction and operation. Through projects such as Mullafarry, SSE continues to play a leading role in Ireland’s energy transition,” Demeuldre said. content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 17 2026 - 8:38 am PT
low-cost Seagull EV, sold as the Dolphin Surf in Europe and Dolphin Mini in other overseas markets, is due for an upgrade. Here’s a sneak peek.
BYD prepares to launch the new Seagull EV
The current 2026 Seagull starts at just 69,900 yuan in China, or about $10,000, making it BYD’s most affordable pure electric vehicle.
It’s also among BYD’s most popular models. According to data compiled by
Cleantechnica
, BYD’s Seagull (Dolphin Mini/Dolphin Surf) was the sixth-best-selling EV globally through the first half of 2026.
With new competition emerging, BYD is preparing to introduce the upgraded Seagull. The new version is expected to roll out in China first, then to overseas markets.
About a month ago, Zhang Zhuo, the sales boss of BYD’s Ocean series,
previewed the new Seagull
for the first time, posting several blurry images on social media.
The caption read, “As its silhouette gradually emerges in the shadows, the promise of growing up is about to be fulfilled. #BYDSseagull#.”
While it’s still blurry, you can see the new version has a LiDAR on the roof to support new ADAS features.
While BYD has yet to announce the details, the new Seagull was released in the batch of new energy vehicles approved for sale by China’s
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
(MIIT) last month, revealing a few new upgrades.
For one, the new Seagull is a bit longer than the current version. According to the release, the upgraded Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm tall, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the current Seagull is just 3,780 mm long.
While the interior was expected to feature BYD’s updated design, a new spy photo from
ThinkerCar
offers a sneak peek.
An alleged spy shot of the all-new
Seagull interior has surfaced. The model is reportedly set for comprehensive upgrades to styling, cabin, dimensions, and powertrain, boosting its competitiveness.
https://t.co/gq4z2Fs9Kd
The upgraded version will also gain a more powerful 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor, up from the 55 kW (75 hp) in the current Seagull.
2026 BYD Seagull EV interior (Source: BYD)
We will have to wait closer to launch to learn battery specs and more details, but the upgraded Seagull will likely be equipped with BYD’s new Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech.
The current 2026 Seagull is available with two battery packs: 30.08 kWh and 38.88 kWh. The former provides a CLTC range of up to 305 km (190 miles), and the latter, 405 km (251 miles).

title: GM offers free charging to more of its Latin American Chevy customers
content:
EV Charging
Chevrolet
South America
Jo Borrás
| Aug 17 2026 - 5:06 am PT
GM’s Latin American expansion continues with news that Chevrolet is offering EV buyers free charging at network at dealerships throughout Peru, where sales of plug-powered vehicles are growing rapidly.
The General is putting serious money into its global EV expansion these days,
with a high-profile launch of the Cadillac brand in South America’s largest car market
followed closely by this week’s news that the company is making its network of dealership charging infrastructure more accessible to its EV customers through in Peru.
In addition to complementing the growing public charging network options being developed throughout the region, the move directly benefits buyers of cars like the slick Chevy Captiva and
chunky Spark EUV
– and there are a
of those.
People like them
Chevy Captiva (left), and Spark EV (right); via GM Authority.
“In the first half of the year, sales of electrified vehicles grew by more than 86 percent in Peru, demonstrating increased consumer interest in these technologies,” said Marketing Manager of GM Peru, Melisa Black. “However, this progress must also be accompanied by more charging options. Therefore, from the outset of our launch plan, we have included the installation of charging points at dealerships that sell these models.”
That translates to an impressive 8,285 plug-in Chevrolets sold in Peru during the first half of the year
, alone – with more to come as the company continues its push into the region with more affordable,
sometimes Chinese-derived EVs
GM Authority
reports that the free chargers are currently available in most of Peru’s major cities, including the capital, Lima, and others in the regions of Arequipa, Cajamarca, Lambayeque, and La Libertad, and are accessible by Chevy customers during regular business hours.
Electrek’s Take
No charging sign, by Steve Birkett.
Don’t get me wrong, here. More charging is good news, and more free charging is great news – especially in a region with less reliable access to energy, of all kinds, than we’ve gotten to enjoy here in the US. That said, auto dealerships (be they here, there, or anywhere in between) are capitalist enterprises, and capitalism has a well-established track record of taking a good thing and finding ways to squeeze profits out of good things.
I wrote a bit more about this a few weeks ago, in a piece titled “
When public charging stations aren’t so public, and why it matters
,” that covered this exact topic from an American perspctive. Give that one a read, then let us know what you think of GM’s plan to get more people comfortable coming to its dealers in the comments.

title: Hyundai opens IONIQ 3 EV orders, starting at about $30,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 17 2026 - 6:57 am PT
opened orders for the IONIQ 3, its new entry-level electric hatch, starting at about $30,000.
Hyundai opens IONIQ 3 orders in the UK and Europe
The IONIQ 3 has received “the highest-ever level of customer interest recorded for a new Hyundai model,”
the company said
last month. That includes gas and electric vehicles.
Hyundai opened orders for the new electric hatch in the UK on Monday, its first compact EV from the IONIQ lineup.
It’s available in four trims: Advance, Premium, Ultimate, and N Line Evo, with standard and extended-range battery options.
The base Hyundai IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the standard 42 kWh battery starts at £22,245, or roughly $30,000. Upgrading to the larger 61 kWh battery starts at £25,745 ($35,000).
Ashley Andrew, President of Hyundai and Genesis UK, said the IONIQ 3 “delivers genuine EV innovation at a price point that makes electric mobility attainable for even more households.”
The Standard trim comes with the 42 kWh battery, offering a WLTP range of up to 213 miles, while the Premium, Ultimate, and N-Line Evo are powered by the 61 kWh battery, which provides up to 308 miles of range.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 (Source: Hyundai)
While it’s positioned as a little sibling to the IONIQ 5, the IONIQ 3 brings a new look to the lineup with Hyundai’s Art of Steel design language.
The new Aero Hatch shape “reimagines the compact EV silhouette,” Hyundai said, delivering a best-in-class drag coefficient of just 0.263. The design is not only extremely aerodynamic, but it also opens up the interior.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 (Source: Hyundai)
Measuring 4,155 mm (163.5″) in length, 1,800 mm (70.9″) in width, and 1,505 mm (59.3″) in height, with a wheelbase of 2,680 mm (105.5″), the IONIQ 3 is even slightly smaller than the Kia EV3 and Chevy Bolt EV.
Despite its compact size, the IONIQ 3 has smart storage throughout the interior, including a “Megabox” underfloor storage.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior (Source: Hyundai)
With a total boot capacity of up to 441 liters, Hyundai said the IONIQ 3 “sets the benchmark in the segment.”
The IONIQ 3 is Hyundai’s first vehicle in Europe and the UK that’s equipped with its new Pleos Connect infotainment system and software.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior with Pleos Connect infotainment system (Source: Hyundai)
Based on Android Automotive OS, the system is more like using a smartphone with apps and customizable screens, similar to what Tesla uses. It’s available with a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen and an optional driver display.
Other features include Hyundai Digital Key 2, Plug & Charge, an integrated EV route planner, and Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) functionality.

title: Not sold on Tesla Powerwall? There are some great home battery alternatives out there
content:
Between increasingly extreme weather, rising electricity demands, and the rapid expansion of data centers, energy independence is starting to look less like a talking point for doomsday preppers and more like sound planning. That shift in thinking is driving more homeowners than ever towards solar-plus-battery energy solutions like the industry-leading Tesla Powerwall – but Powerwall isn’t the only game in town, anymore.
Maybe you’re avoiding Tesla products because of Elon Musk’s political antics, or maybe it’s Tesla’s recent recalls that have given you pause, or maybe you just want to see what else is out there. Whatever the reason, there are more compelling home battery options than ever – and they’ve got enough high-tech features packed into ’em that keeping the lights on in a storm might be the least interesting thing they can do.
As I was putting this list together, I realized there were plenty of ways for me to present this list. “Best batteries ..?” Too opinion-based. “Cheapest batteries ..?” Too much research and a quick descent into Temu-grade nonsense. In the end, I went with the same solution I’ve been using on my 0% EV financing lists: alphabetical order, by brand.
Anker SOLIX X1
The Anker SOLIX X1 is built to be highly modular. Starting out with a relatively modest 5 kWh of energy storage from a single low-profile LiFePO4 battery, the X1 system allows owners to stack storage and scale up all the way up to 180 kWh. That flexibility makes it a particularly interesting option for homeowners who are sold on the concept of a home battery but not quite sure how far down the rabbit hole they want to go. With Anker SOLIX X1, they can meet their most critical needs on day one, and build up to a system that can support their wants later.
The X1 also adds some thoughtful backup features, including automatic storm preparation and a 20 millisecond automative switchover time, while its IP66-rated weatherproof enclosure and 10-year warranty are reassuring for something that’s supposed to sit outside and keep your house running when the grid doesn’t.
BLUETTI EP800
The portable power experts at BLUETTI have put together another modular home battery system built around the company’s EP800 inverter and modular B500 battery packs. A basic two-battery configuration provides 9.92 kWh of storage, while additional packs can push total capacity to nearly 40 kWh and 7.6 kW of output.
The EP800 can work with rooftop solar panels or microinverters, but BLUETTI designed it to also be able to charge from the grid during cheaper off-peak hours, stockpiling that energy for when rates rise. That means you get backup power and time-of-use savings without needing rooftop solar, making the EP800 a compelling case for renters or homeowners who aren’t quite ready to make the jump to a full solar-plus-storage system.
Enphase IQ Battery 5P
If you’re looking for a one-brand solution for EV charging and whole-home battery backup but don’t want to be “locked in” to GM or Tesla’s ecosystem, Enphase offers a full line of battery solutions that might be what you’re looking for.
Described as a full off-grid system, Enphase batteries let homeowners power their homes without a utility connection, even for extended periods. It works by combining the Enphase IQ Battery 5P with IQ8 series microinverters with Sunlight JumpStart, and a third-party standby AC generator.
“Energy systems developer Enphase Energy is providing an even more holistic approach to managing home power usage with the introduction of new EV charger technology called the IQ line,” wrote Scooter doll, when the brand first introduced its EV charging solutions back in 2023. “The Enphase IQ is Wi-Fi enabled and integrates seamlessly into a customer’s existing home system that can be controlled with your phone.”
FranklinWH aPower S
Fans of the Tesla Powerwall often point to its sleek, integrated design as one of the things that’s most appealing about it. The FranklinWH aPower S takes a similarly clean, minimalist approach, packing the battery and inverter into a single unit and simplifying installation. Each aPower S unit stores 15 kWh of usable energy and can deliver up to 10 kW of continuous power, while multiple aPower batteries can be combined for larger homes or higher energy needs.
The aPower S can also be wired into existing solar installations and be controlled virtually as part of a larger VPP scheme, making it a particularly flexible option for homeowners who already have solar and simply to add storage to their existing solution.
We got a chance to speak with FranklinWH CEO Gary Lam about the scalability of his home battery solutions. You can check out that episode, above.
GM Energy Home System
Arguably the most fully integrated EV + battery backup + solar option out there, the GM Energy Home System promises to do everything a conventional home solar battery does, plus the ability work seamlessly with your GM EV to provide even more flexibility and energy independence – whether that means using the electric fuel stored in your EV to hold out that much longer in an emergency, or using the energy stored in your home’s solar battery to power an escape in your electric Chevrolet is up to you.
GM Energy and GM’s car dealers list Qmerit as their installation partner. They’re great, but if you already “have a guy,” you can order the 10.6 kWh Home System directly from GM Energy’s website for as little as $11,897 (as I type this).
Sigenergy V2X
As some of the earliest and most enthusiastic EV adopters, Tesla fans have also been among the loudest advocates for using the energy stored their cars’ batteries to back up their homes — or even the grid itself. Unfortunately for them, the slow-selling Cybertruck is the only Tesla vehicle that officially supports bi-directional charging. If you’re one of the many Model 3 and Y owners frustrated by those delays, there’s good news: those vehicles are now capable of V2H charging thanks to an “impressive” Powerwall competitor, Sigenergy.
The good news doesn’t stop with the Tesla cars, however. The Sigenergy V2X also works with a number of popular EV models over the DIN70121 protocol, and several VW/Audi/Porsche and Mercedes-Benz models over the ISO15118-2 protocol.
Our Editor-in-Chief, Fred Lambert, recently went on a Sigenergy deep dive with Sylvain Juteau, President of Roulez Electrique, and came away deeply impressed with the system. I’ve included the video, above, and you can read more about the system itself at this link
Villara VillaGrid+
I’m not an electrician, a chemical engineer, or someone who’s researched thousands of home battery installations. That’s why this isn’t a “best batteries” post, after all – but our friends and solar industry experts at EnergySage, though? They’re all three of those things, and they really, really like the Villara VillaGrid+.
“The Villara VillaGrid+ stands out as the best battery on the market, scoring highest in EnergySage’s rigorous Equipment Rating System, explains EnergySage’s Kristina Zagame. “That said, (the Villara VillaGrid+) is not necessarily the best Tesla Powerwall alternative. It’s a very different (and much pricier) battery.”
What makes the VillaGrid+ worth the price premium? According to Zagame, it all comes down to the battery’s lithium-titanium-oxide, or LTO chemistry. “Unlike more traditional lithium-ion batteries, LTO has better recharge capabilities for longer life cycles, and doesn’t contain any carbon, which makes it extra safe. The downside is you’ll definitely shell out more money upfront for the VillaGrid+.”
Top comment by joegoesbananas
I have a triple-Powerwall and solar setup installed by Tesla, and I highly recommend buying an alternative product. The Tesla batteries themselves aren't the problem, it's their inverter/gateway design. We are on our second inverter (already also dying; first one lasted less than a year), and our second gateway. Tesla designed the inverters with zero airflow. There is a small fan inside and a tiny grill, but the grill is at the bottom, is comically small, and the fan doesn't point at it, so no hot air can escape. The fan screams while it recirculates trapped scorching air until the inverter repeatedly turns off due to overheating, and eventually fails completely. You have to prop the cover open if you don't want to lose DC power sources every time the weather goes over 95 degrees (and my unit is north-facing and is completely shaded). When your system dies, expect at least a month before they will fix it, and that's after they ignore you, argue with you, don't call back, make you do the same troubleshooting steps multiple times, etc. For a system that one buys to reduce worry and stress, our Tesla Powerwall system has caused us an awful lot of worry and stress.
That extra money will also buy some additional peace of mind, as Villara backs its LTO batteries with a 20-year warranty compared to Tesla Powerwall and its (and just about everyone else’s) 10-year deal. I couldn’t find a price, but Villara’s other products, like VillaGrid 5.75 kWh battery, come in at nearly double the Powerwall’s per kWh cost.

title: Tesla FSD v14 swerved and try to drive me into a ditch for no reason
content:
Full Self-Driving (FSD)
Fred Lambert
| Aug 17 2026 - 7:14 am PT
Tesla’s Full Self-Driving v14.3.6 tried to take a highway exit that my car had already passed, at 110 km/h (68 mph), and it would have taken us straight into the ditch.
I was ready to take control, and I did, but it was scary. My girlfriend, sitting in the passenger seat, screamed in fear.
What the dashcam shows
This was Sunday night on Autoroute 55 in Quebec’s Mauricie region, running FSD (Supervised) v14.3.6 — the latest and greatest Tesla FSD build on the latest hardware.
The car is cruising at 110 km/h in the right lane. Dry pavement, no traffic in either direction, fresh painted lines, reflective overhead signage. Perfect conditions for FSD. As we pass under the gantry for exit 217, the right turn signal comes on and the car starts pulling toward the shoulder, still showing “Self-Driving” on the screen.
The problem is that the ramp was already peeling off behind us. It was going to drive us straight into the ditch by turning this late at that speed.
The speed readout goes 110, 109, 107, 104 as it commits to the maneuver. That’s when I grabbed the wheel. “Self-Driving” drops off the display at 102 km/h.
This wasn’t a lane-position wobble or a moment of hesitation. The car decided to put its blinker on and take an exit it had no business taking
These were ideal conditions for FSD
If you were designing the easiest possible scenario for Tesla’s system, this was it.
Divided highway. Night, so oncoming headlights and lane reflectors are easy to pick out. Zero traffic to reason about. Crisp lane markings. Big, well-lit signage.
Based on everything I’ve seen from v14, highway driving at night on an empty road is where the system is at its absolute best. I’ve done thousands of kilometres of exactly this without touching anything. Which is why I was confident. And that confidence is the whole trap.
I wrote about this exact risk in June
Two and a half months ago I published a piece arguing that
FSD v14 is so good it’s making me dangerously complacent
. I wrote then that “a system that works
perfectly creates a trap — drivers trust it just enough to stop paying attention, but it still fails unpredictably and sometimes critically.”
I stand by every word, and Sunday night was the demonstration. A couple thousand miles between critical interventions is genuinely impressive engineering. It’s also exactly the interval that teaches your brain to stop scanning.
Tesla’s own v14.3.6 release notes say the company “upgraded the Reinforcement Learning (RL) stage of training the FSD neural network,” rewrote the AI compiler with MLIR for “20% faster reaction time,” and improved the car’s response to system degradations, “reducing unnecessary disengagements.” Disengagements go down when the software gets better, and they also go down when the driver stops intervening. Tesla doesn’t publish anything that lets outsiders tell those two apart.
And the public numbers that do exist aren’t reassuring. Tesla reported
a record 207 Autopilot and FSD crashes to NHTSA in a single month
, with the narrative redacted on 99.9% of its 3,763 driver-assist crash reports since 2019. Musk is still telling investors that
unsupervised FSD will be widespread in the US by year-end
Waymo’s co-CEO keeps explaining why camera-only self-driving falls short
of what a driverless system actually needs.
Electrek’s Take
One near-miss is an anecdote, not data, but I think it’s an important reminder to stay attentive.
As I have often said, Tesla FSD v14 is a truly impressive product. Sure, it falls apart when compared to what FSD was originally sold as: becoming unsupervised self-driving. It’s not close to that and might never be. That will remain a problem and probably the worst move Tesla has ever done.
But if you set that aside and look at FSD as a point-to-point driver-assist system, it is truly incredible.
However, it is so incredible now that it breeds complacency. Tesla doesn’t help with CEO Elon Musk saying things like “you can look at your phone now while using it.”
This is obviously reckless. As the system gets better, Tesla needs to get better at convincing drivers to pay attention because of this complacency issue. Not the other way around.

title: 思源电气：2026年H1储能业务营收同比增长231%
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，8月14日晚，思源电气披露2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入107.95亿元，同比增长27.05%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润14.64亿元，同比增长13.23%；扣非后净利润13.98亿元，同比增长13.12%。
单季度表现来看，思源电气二季度业绩较一季度明显回升。公司一季度实现营业收入45.69亿元，归母净利润5.50亿元，扣非净利润4.93亿元；根据半年报数据测算，二季度实现营业收入约62.27亿元，环比增长36.29%；归母净利润约9.14亿元，环比增长66.15%，扣非净利润9.06亿元，环比增长83.89%。
储能成为思源电气上半年增长最快的业务。报告期内，公司储能系统及元件类业务实现收入13.91亿元，同比增长231.25%，占营业收入比重由上年同期的4.94%提升至12.89%；毛利率为10.50%，同比提升4.22%。
与此同时，EPC业务收入11.17亿元，同比增长38.42%。传统输配电业务中，开关类、变压器类和保护及自动化类业务收入分别同比增长22.46%、12.46%和15.80%。
海外市场仍是公司重要收入来源。2026年上半年，思源电气海外地区实现营业收入31.83亿元，同比增长11.22%，占公司总营收的29.49%。截至目前，公司业务已覆盖全球100多个国家和地区，并在巴西、埃及、赞比亚、西班牙、瑞士等20多个国家设立子公司。
整体来看，2026年上半年思源电气业绩增长主要来自输配电主业稳步扩张以及储能业务快速放量。其中，储能业务收入同比增长超过两倍，业务占比明显提升，成为公司新的业绩增长点；与此同时，公司持续加码研发、储能产能及海外市场，业务结构正进一步向新型电力系统及储能等领域延伸。

title: 晶科/TCL中环/正泰获超300MW组件订单
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，光伏市场订单与项目建设持续推进。晶科能源、TCL中环分别斩获组件订单，正泰新能源承建的新西兰170MW光伏项目实现并网。
晶科能源中标133.36MW组件采购项目
近日，晶科能源中标国家能源湖南公司2026年（第一批次）光伏组件采购项目，将为鹭滋湖渔光互补发电项目和正阳（杨桥）复合型光伏发电项目供应133.36MW高效光伏组件。
据了解，鹭滋湖项目为渔光互补项目，建设场景以坑塘水域为主；正阳（杨桥）项目为复合型光伏项目，主要位于低山丘陵地区。
本次中标项目将采用晶科能源Tiger Neo 3（飞虎3）系列组件，用于满足不同应用场景下的发电需求。
TCL中环中标京能库布齐沙漠光伏项目
近日，TCL中环中标内蒙古京能准旗新能源有限公司库布齐沙漠基地光伏项目，将为项目提供N型BC光伏组件。
据了解，项目位于内蒙古库布齐沙漠基地，属于国家“沙戈荒”大型风电光伏基地建设项目，兼具光伏发电与生态治沙功能。
TCL中环表示，本次项目将采用其N型BC技术路线产品，以满足沙漠场景下的发电及长期运行需求。
正泰新能源承建新西兰170MW光伏项目并网
近日，由正泰新能源担任EPC总包方承建的新西兰Kōwhai 170MWdc光伏项目成功并网发电。
项目位于新西兰克赖斯特彻奇机场附近，是目前新西兰单体规模最大的光伏电站之一。作为EPC总包方，正泰新能源负责项目设计、采购和施工。
据了解，该项目采用正泰新能ASTRO N5系列光伏组件，并按照当地环保法规实施生态监测和植被保护措施，最终实现按期并网。

Bookmark
A Japanese power firm will explore deploying a turquoise hydrogen plant based on technology from Australia’s Hazer Group.
Through a memorandum of understanding, Hazer and its engineering partner KBR will complete a paid pre-feasibility study for an unnamed “tier-1” company, assessing the use of plants producing 30,000 and 300,000 tonnes of hydrogen per year.
The study, which comes as the first commercial engagement since Hazer and KBR completed a joint
hydrogen plant design
in April, is expected to be completed this year.
The design uses Hazer’s methane pyrolysis technology, which splits methane into hydrogen and solid carbon in an oxygen-free environment using an iron ore catalyst.
Details of how the unnamed company would use hydrogen to generate power were not disclosed.
Glenn Corrie, CEO of Hazer, claimed the study confirmed “strong application potential” for Hazer’s technology in the Japanese market, claiming it could deliver “scalable, commercially competitive low-emission hydrogen to the clean power sector.”
Proponents praise methane pyrolysis for offering a potentially low-emission hydrogen production pathway with a commercial byproduct in solid carbon.
However, critics warn the pathway could worsen upstream greenhouse gas emissions in some cases, using more natural gas than steam methane reforming and risking methane leaks if fossil gas is the feedstock.
For the power sector, there will be particular concern around efficiency losses from the pathway compared to combusting natural gas.
The move also comes as the Asia-Pacific region pays increasing attention to hydrogen and derivatives for power applications.
A duo including energy company Korea South-East Power recently
revealed plans
to set up a 320MW electrolyser and 100MW hydrogen-fuelled power plant in South Korea’s coastal region.
In April, Singapore’s Energy Market Authority opened a
call for proposals
for three hydrogen-ready gas power plants to be online in 2032.

title: AirTag 挖出亚马逊训练 AI“毁书”手段：为提高扫描效率，先把书脊切掉
content:
感谢IT之家网友
8 月 17 日消息，亚马逊正大批购入纸质书籍，将内容扫描后用于训练 AI，并在扫描过程中
当地时间 17 日，外媒 404 Media 公布了一次追踪调查：调查人员把苹果 AirTag
藏进一批珍贵书籍的货件
中，一路追踪这些书在美国境内的去向。
货件最终抵达亚马逊位于拉斯维加斯的一座仓库。仓库内有一支名为 VGT3 的团队，标志是一只手拿书本的霸王龙。员工称，为了提高扫描效率，他们会先切掉书脊，
因此原书会在处理过程中被毁
。亚马逊随后使用扫描得到的数据训练 Nova 模型。亚马逊发言人称，公司
通过正常商业渠道采购书籍
，用于改进产品。
一些书商怀疑，AI 公司正在尝试按照 ISBN 编号，系统性地逐本扫描出版过的书籍。纸质书的价值尤其高，因为很多内容从未出现在互联网上，
而且大量书籍出版于 2022 年以前，不含 AI 生成内容
据IT之家了解，采取这种方式的并不只有亚马逊。Anthropic 此前也曾进行类似项目。图书作者提起的一起诉讼披露了 Anthropic 内部的“巴拿马计划”：
公司从电商平台购入书籍，切除书脊，再将内容数字化
审理该案的法官裁定，这类扫描属于合理使用，不构成版权侵权。裁决的一项依据是
纸质原件已经被销毁
，因此不存在原书复制后再出售的情况。
亚马逊和 Anthropic 都在把部分珍贵书籍转化为企业私有的 AI 训练材料。争议在于，一些被毁掉的原书可能根本无法替代，原本能够
留在公共书架上的知识
也随之消失，最终只被封存在
单一公司的封闭 AI 模型内部

content:
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，LG 电子今天（17 日）发布了 xboom Power 系列旗舰派对音箱，内置高功率音响、智能技术和“AI 卡拉 OK 大师”，全系采用 xboom 的“标志性”音效，并由多次获得格莱美奖的音乐人 will.i.am 参与调校，在保持声音清晰均衡的基础上强化低频冲击力，营造更适合派对的听感。
该系列包含 Power 9000、Power 7000 和 Power 5000 三款型号，分别对应不同规模和使用场景的聚会。
- LG xboom Power 9000： 系列旗舰，主要面向大型派对和户外活动，持续输出功率 440W，可以覆盖更大的活动空间。
- LG xboom Power 7000： 主要面向大型聚会、露台和户外娱乐场景，持续输出功率 340W，兼顾性能、易用性和场景适应能力。
- LG xboom Power 5000： 面向家庭聚会、日常庆祝活动和规模较小的社交场合，持续输出功率 260W，以更紧凑的机身提供卡拉 OK、动态派对灯效和高品质音效。
新品全系标配多彩 AI 灯效和 DJ 表演效果，提供智能支架，可以放置智能手机或平板电脑显示歌词。此外，其标配双麦克风输入，可以让两个人同时演唱。
该产品还内置“AI 卡拉 OK 大师”和其他互动功能，用户可以直接把自己音乐库中的歌曲转换成卡拉 OK 伴奏，并调整音调或去除人声。具体来看，其支持 AI 消除人声、变调、一键启动。
IT之家获悉，LG xboom Power 系列还能够根据音乐类型和使用环境自动优化音效。AI 音效能分析正在播放的内容，并根据音乐类型自动调整声音设置，提供更有针对性的聆听效果。
此外，其能够根据所在空间的大小和布局调整声音输出，让音箱在室内和户外环境中都能适应现场条件。该系列音箱还支持 Auracast，把 xboom 家族中的多台兼容音箱连接起来，实现同步播放并扩大声音覆盖范围。

title: Uber 与 Zipline 达成合作，年内在美国推出无人机送外卖服务
content:
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，据科技媒体 The Verge 今天报道，Uber（优步）现已与美国无人机配送公司 Zipline 达成合作，计划今年晚些时候在美国启动无人机配送外卖服务。
Uber 目前已对 Zipline 进行战略投资。双方计划在美国得州沃思堡推出 Uber Eats 无人机配送服务，随后逐步扩展到美国数十个城市。
IT之家从原报道了解到，Zipline 的无人机也在几分钟内将顾客订购的餐品送到住宅前院。Uber 则在打造人类、无人机混合的配送网络，系统会根据顾客所在位置，自动选择最高效的送餐模式。
未来，消费者将可以使用 Uber Eats 应用下单美食，再由无人机完成配送。相比传统配送方式，无人机理论上能够避开道路交通，并缩短配送时间。

title: 《方舟：生存进化》Switch 版官方服务器本月关闭，玩家需转向私服或离线模式
content:
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，开发商 Studio Wildcard 今天确认，《方舟：生存进化》Switch 版游戏官方线上服务器将于本月底关闭。
IT之家了解到，《方舟：生存进化》最初于 2017 年登陆 PC、PS4 和 Xbox One 平台，随后于 2018 年推出 Switch 版，该版本的游戏最初由于性能表现糟糕，遭受玩家和媒体批评。
2022 年，Grove Street Games 为 Switch 平台带来了《方舟：终极幸存者版》，原版玩家可免费升级。
据 Studio Wildcard 所述，《方舟：生存进化》和《方舟：终极幸存者版》的官方线上服务器都将在 8 月 13 日停止服务。如果玩家仍希望游玩线上内容，则需要连接非官方的私人服务器。已购买游戏的玩家仍然可以进入离线模式，游玩单人模式。

title: 佛州一男子向 ChatGPT 描述“杀害前女友”计划，OpenAI 报案了
content:
8 月 17 日消息，据《今日美国》当地时间 14 日报道，OpenAI 向 FBI 举报了一名 25 岁的佛罗里达州男子达伦 · 周，原因是他曾向 ChatGPT
详细描述强奸并杀害前女友的计划
法庭记录显示，达伦 · 周曾对 ChatGPT 称：“我会在这个月底之前杀了她。如果我得不到她，那谁也别想得到她。”
达伦 · 周是一名被解雇的高盛分析师。今年 3 月，他开始通过 ChatGPT 倾诉自己
与交往六个月的女友刚刚分手
一事，谈到了女方的兴趣爱好和经常前往的地点，也描述了自己对女方身边其他男性的嫉妒，以及希望复合的想法。
按照 OpenAI 的政策，如果系统发现用户可能计划伤害他人，一个小组就可以
审查该用户与 ChatGPT 的互动
。情况严重时，OpenAI 可能
直接向执法部门提供线索
ChatGPT 聊天记录已经在不少司法案件中被用作证据，但
由 OpenAI 主动把用户活动举报给警方
的情况仍然少见。
调查人员称，达伦 · 周的信息很快从讨论分手
转变为强奸、谋杀以及杀人后自杀的威胁
今年 5 月，联邦探员把当事人两个月的 ChatGPT 聊天记录
交给棕榈滩县警长办公室
。此时，达伦 · 周威胁的对象已经
扩大到前女友的家人
。一名查看记录的警员称，材料只保留了达伦 · 周发送的信息，没有 ChatGPT 的回复，而内容并不是“模糊的情绪宣泄”，反而体现出
反复演练和制定计划
警方随后上门确认女方是否安全。女方 21 岁，来自莱克沃思比奇。她透露，达伦 · 周长期表现出“反复无常、嫉妒心强和控制欲强的行为”，因此自己决定分手。由于担心对方的反应，
她甚至不敢当面提出
，只选择通过电话结束关系。
女方称，分手以后，达伦 · 周不断通过电话、短信和社交媒体信息纠缠她，还反复追问一名男子在她 TikTok 视频下留下的评论。
调查人员称，达伦 · 周随后继续
使用不同应用生成的电话号码
联系前女友。女方保存了大量信息截图，其中许多内容带有
骚扰、侮辱、性意味和威胁性质
IT之家获悉，警方掌握达伦 · 周发给 AI 和前女友的信息后，于今年 5 月将其逮捕。助理州检察官安娜 · 库斯科娃今年 6 月以加重跟踪骚扰、书面死亡威胁和非法使用手机三项重罪起诉达伦 · 周，最高刑期可达 25 年。
经过协商，达伦 · 周于当地时间 8 月 13 日对三项指控全部认罪，换取
无需入狱且不留下重罪定罪记录
的协议。按照协议，法院暂缓作出有罪裁定，达伦 · 周被判 8 年缓刑，期间必须遵守多项限制。

title: 保时捷北美 CEO：只要法规允许、市场还有需求，我们会尽可能推出手动挡车型
content:
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，保时捷北美 CEO 蒂莫 · 雷施称，只要法规允许、市场还有需求，公司就会尽可能继续生产手动挡车型。
雷施在蒙特雷汽车周接受美媒《Road & Track》采访时重申：“可以肯定的是，只要法律允许，而且客户还有需求，我们就会尽可能长时间地提供手动变速箱。”
未来法规会允许手动挡延续多久，雷施无法预测，不过市场需求至少让保时捷相当乐观。“我们看到，客户对手动变速箱的需求还会持续到 2030 年代相当长一段时间。”
雷施指出，消费者此前一直希望保时捷在基础版 Carrera T 和 GT3 之间增加一款“三踏板（IT之家注：刹车、油门、离合器）”车型，于是有了新款手动挡 Carrera S。新车搭载 473 马力水平对置六缸发动机，性能定位正好位于 389 马力的 Carrera T 和 503 马力的 GT3 之间。
按照保时捷自己的车型统计方式，911 Carrera S 和 Carrera T 算不同车型，硬顶版与敞篷版也分别计算，公司目前共有 7 款手动挡车型。若按更常见的方式来看，其实可以算作 3 款 911，分别是 Carrera S、Carrera T 和 GT3。
北美消费者对手动挡也并非“叫好不叫座”。雷施透露，超过一半的 GT3 买家实际选择了手动变速箱，若看 GT3 Touring，比例更高达 80%。“我们的态度就是，没错，驾驶体验更重要。”

title: 字节跳动与美国电影协会签署协议，加强 AI 模型版权保护
content:

字节跳动和美国电影协会表示，双方将在 AI 不断发展的同时，继续完善版权防护措施。

title: 小鹏 G9L 麋鹿测试时速超 80 公里，成功挑战同级最快通过速度
content:
感谢IT之家网友 Autumn_Dream 的线索投递！
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，小鹏汽车官方今日宣布，小鹏 G9L 麋鹿测试时速超 80 公里，成功挑战同级最快通过速度。该车宣称全系标配百万级旗舰底盘，支持极端情况瞬间稳住车身。
据IT之家此前报道，小鹏 G9L 汽车已于 8 月 11 日开启预售，共推出超级增程、纯电两种动力，预售价 25.98 万元。
外观方面，小鹏 G9L 拥有普罗旺斯紫、托斯卡纳绿、珠峰白、峡湾灰、极夜黑等多款车色可选，车身尺寸为 5120mm*1999mm*1782mm，拥有 3100mm 的超长轴距和 0.605 轴长比。搭载行业首创前后双贯穿灯，配备 480 颗独立 LED 灯珠，尾部采用溜背造型，凸显年轻化姿态。
座舱方面，小鹏 G9L 首发智能四电机行政中岛，它支持语音、按键、屏幕三种方式开启小桌板，并能随座椅靠背自动调平。扶手集成 50W 风冷无线快充与双隐藏杯托，桌板自带手机支架与化妆镜，搭配吸顶屏秒变私人影院，支持 220V 供电。
动力方面，该车提供超级增程、纯电两种版本，全系标配 800V 高压超快充平台。增程版均搭载四驱，纯电续航可达 435km、综合续航 1602km；纯电版最高续航最高可达 755km，可选四驱。

title: 开发风火轮小车、芭比娃娃的玩具巨头要开发游戏了，美泰宣布成立游戏工作室
content:
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，据外媒 Game Developer 今天（17 日）报道，玩具制造商美泰旗下的美泰游戏工作室正式成立，今后将负责开发、发行和运营基于旗下品牌打造的游戏。
美泰游戏工作室隶属于美泰数字工作室，后者统筹美泰自主发行游戏、品牌授权项目等一系列更广泛的数字游戏业务。据悉，新部门将整合洛杉矶和杭州近 300 名游戏业务员工。
美泰游戏工作室将接手现有手游产品组合，同时发行新的免费手游。除了传统手游业务，美泰还准备通过新部门在 Roblox 和《堡垒之夜》等热门用户生成内容平台上推出原创游戏体验。
对于拥有芭比、风火轮、UNO、《宇宙巨人希曼》、Polly Pocket 和《托马斯和朋友》等知名 IP 的美泰而言，成立专门的游戏工作室是一项值得关注的业务调整。
不久前，美泰刚以 3.18 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 21.46 亿元人民币）估值从网易手中收购手游工作室 Mattel163。Mattel163 目前运营《UNO!》《UNO Wonder》《Phase 10》和《Skip》等手游。自 2018 年以来，这些游戏全球累计下载量已经超过 5.5 亿次，月活跃玩家约 2000 万。
美泰数字工作室全球负责人马库斯 · 利亚西德斯宣布，公司决心推出更多以旗下标志性品牌为灵感的原创游戏体验。
目前，美泰游戏工作室正在开发一款新的风火轮游戏，并准备试运营新作《UNO Wild》。

title: 新一代奔驰 C 级车全球首发：首搭 S 级同款发光格栅、Momenta R7 智驾，宣称史上最全面技术升级
content:
IT之家 8 月 17 日消息，梅赛德斯-奔驰官方微博今日宣布，新一代 C 级车全球首发。
据介绍，自 1982 年问世以来，C 级车累计销量已突破 1,200 万辆。新一代 C 级车将迎来史上最全面技术升级，拥有更多 S 级旗舰同源科技。
外观方面，新一代 C 级车首度搭载 S 级同款发光格栅，星徽头灯与尾灯前后呼应，智能数字大灯光线照射更精准通透，可规避夜间行车视野盲区。打开车门，外后视镜将投射三叉星徽点亮地面。
内饰方面，新车搭载优化升级的 Burmester 3D 环绕立体声音响系统，支持杜比全景声，并配备 15 个扬声器；全新多功能方向盘，采用拨杆与滚轮等物理控制，方便高频操作。
智能方面，新一代 C 级车基于奔驰自研 MB.OS 架构打造，支持持续迭代 OTA；豆包 AI 大模型等将融入智能座舱；针对中国复杂交通环境，新车搭载与 Momenta 共同研发的中国专属城区及高速领航辅助驾驶系统，已实现“全国都能开”，未来在国内上市时，还将搭载 Momenta R7“世界模型”。
驾控方面，新车搭载新款 2.0 升 M 254 EVO 四缸汽油发动机搭载第二代智能电机系统，可提供最高 17 千瓦额外功率及 205 牛 · 米额外扭矩；48 伏电气系统支持滑行与能量回收，城区通勤频繁启停与长距离巡航更高效、平顺；全新电动辅助增压器支持毫秒级建立增压，起步与再加速更敏捷；专属优化悬挂系统，保留长途舒适性。
IT之家注：此次奔驰官方分享的配置信息为全球配置及数据，具体车型配置及数据以未来中国实际上市车型为准。

content:
8 月 17 日消息，本月早些时候，长期准确爆料硬件和游戏消息的 Dealabs 撰稿人 billbil-kun 称，《暗黑破坏神 4》Switch 2 版已接近开发完成。
而在今天（17 日），billbil-kun 更新了此前的爆料，进一步披露发售日期和 DLC 等信息。按照爆料，《暗黑破坏神 4》Switch 2 版计划于
9 月 15 日发售，售价 69.99 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 472.3 元人民币）
Switch 2 版据称将直接推出“憎恨时代”合集，内容包括《暗黑破坏神 4》本体，以及《憎恨之躯》和《憎恨之王》两部资料片。
billbil-kun 还重申，此前所说的实体版确实存在，
但包装盒内只会提供下载码
，不包含游戏卡带或游戏钥匙卡。
游戏具体会在什么时候正式公布，目前仍不确定。billbil-kun 称，消息来源显示预购将在 9 月 12 日开放，而当天
恰好是暴雪嘉年华 2026 开幕日
。按照上述时间安排，《暗黑破坏神 4》Switch 2 版有可能在暴雪嘉年华首日正式公布，随后立即开放预购。
另一个可能的公布时间是 8 月 25 日举行的科隆游戏展开幕之夜直播活动。暴雪已经连续三年亮相科隆游戏展开幕之夜直播活动。2023 年，暴雪在活动中公布《暗黑破坏神 4》“血之赛季”；2024 年发布《暗黑破坏神 4：憎恨之躯》预告片；去年则正式公布《魔兽世界：至暗之夜》。
《暗黑破坏神》系列负责人罗德 · 弗格森早在 2025 年 4 月就透露，
Switch 2 的性能足以运行《暗黑破坏神 4》，
真正需要解决的是服务型游戏的运行方式，因为 Switch 2 经常会以掌机模式使用，玩家有时也无法保持持续联网。

content:

从目前消费电子行业的形势来看，索尼 PS6 的发售日期将根据内存、芯片等零件的供应情况是否好转。

title: How much hydrogen awaits us underground?
content:
How much hydrogen awaits us underground?
The global gold rush for underground stores of hydrogen fuel continues. But researchers are still sorting out how much of the stuff there is.
In the 1990s, Barbara Sherwood Lollar descended into the Kidd Creek mine in northern Ontario, which cuts more than three kilometers into the ancient root of North America. There her team of geochemists found water that had been confined underground for more than a billion years. This ancient brine turned out to be a habitat for living microbes that feed on the hydrogen produced in reactions between the water and the rock.
Decades later, Sherwood Lollar, who is a geochemist at the University of Toronto, revisited the team’s hydrogen data to see if there is enough of the gas in the mine to make it a useful source of zero-carbon fuel. “If we can set some smart minds into figuring out how to hook it up and use it, then we’ve got a win for this nascent economy,” she says.
While hydrogen fuel does show promise as a versatile power source, producing it typically generates lots of greenhouse-gas emissions and requires more energy than the gas contains. The ability to tap ready-made underground reservoirs—so-called “geologic hydrogen”—would change the equation.
A flurry of exploration efforts have launched to search for the stuff, which is produced underground when water molecules are split by chemical reactions with iron-rich rock or—as they are at Kidd Creek—by the radioactive decay of other elements. The hunt has spread all over the world and engaged dozens of startups, including the Australian firm HyTerra and the Bill Gates–backed company Koloma, which have both been poking around the US Midwest to reach ancient oceanic rocks associated with hydrogen production.
Researchers at the US Geological Survey have estimated that trillions of tons of H2 are produced within Earth’s crust; if a small fraction of this could be recovered, it could meet global hydrogen demand for centuries. But the search so far has come up short. No one has yet reported finding a commercially viable reservoir of the gas, and public data on what has been found remains in short supply as companies jockey for position and seek to attract investment.
At Kidd Creek mine, Sherwood Lollar and her colleague Oliver Warr leveraged their long-term record of hydrogen to get a fresh read on the potential. By scrutinizing data they’d collected from 35 boreholes at the mine over more than a decade, they found that each one consistently released an average of eight kilograms of hydrogen per year. Extrapolating that finding to the more than 14,000 boreholes at Kidd Creek would mean that around 140 metric tons of the gas is flowing unused out of the mine’s vents each year.
This tally, published earlier this year in the journal PNAS, is not a world-changing amount, but Sherwood Lollar says that if all the hydrogen could be captured, it would offer at least a modest source of energy—perhaps enough to power a substantial portion of the mine’s operations. That would be a valuable local demonstration that geologic hydrogen really can be put to use, she says.
The results from Kidd Creek add to “the growing evidence that natural hydrogen generation and migration are genuine geological processes,” says Laurent Truche, a geochemist at the University of Grenoble Alpes in France. In 2024, his research team reported that at least 200 metric tons of the gas flow out of the Bulqizë chromium mine in Albania every year. “The remaining challenge is not proving that natural hydrogen exists, but proving that it can be produced economically and reliably at commercial scale,” Truche says.
Proof, however, doesn’t necessarily require striking the mother lode. Researchers and startups are also exploring the possibility of stimulating hydrogen production by injecting water, heat, or catalysts into the reactive rocks that naturally produce the gas. More than a dozen of these projects are funded by ARPA-E, which has established a goal of accelerating the hydrogen-producing reaction by a factor of 10,000—the rate at which, researchers estimate, stimulated H2 production would be commercially viable.
An indication that this could work came earlier this year from the mountains of Oman, where a team drilled a one-kilometer borehole and injected 50,000 cubic meters of water into the rock. When they opened the well several months later, gas was spewing out—and it was 90% hydrogen. “It’s bubbling with gas,” Jo Shannon, a geoscientist at the University of Southampton in the UK, told attendees of the European Geosciences Union conference in May. (Shannon declined to comment beyond what was presented.)
While Shannon said this was a promising sign, she was careful to add that a slew of unknowns remain. The most crucial question is a basic one: Is the hydrogen rising up out of the well made through stimulation, or had it been there all along?

The Download: dead robot friends and the “censorship-industrial complex”
Plus: The US plans to force partners to pick sides in the AI race.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
What happens when a kid’s robot best friend dies?
When Xander first met Moxie, she taught him how to calm down when he was anxious or mad. Six years later, she mostly watches him play Minecraft and talks to him about his stuffed animals.
Moxie is a robot—a 15-inch-tall device that looks a bit like a blue, legless astronaut. It belongs to a subset of robots designed to assist neurodivergent children by providing connection and helping kids practice social skills usually learned from therapists.
Xander still uses Moxie when he feels like he needs someone to talk to, but the device has had a troubled life. The robot’s maker went out of business, its servers were shut down, and parents rushed to convert their Moxies before the servers went offline.
Read our story about how it exposes the promise and pitfalls of AI companion toys for children.
—Sara Harrison
