title: House Bill Would Put Federal Electricity Tax on Data Centers
content:
A new House bill would impose a federal excise tax on electricity consumed by data centers, targeting facilities with more than 1 MW of power capacity and directing the resulting revenue toward five federal funds.
Rep. Andrea Salinas, D-Ore., has introduced the
Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026
, which would amend the Internal Revenue Code to establish a 1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour federal excise tax on electricity used by qualifying data centers. The measure was referred to the House Ways and Means Committee, with additional referrals to the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee.
The proposal comes as rapidly expanding AI and cloud computing workloads are driving
large increases in electricity demand
and intensifying debates over who should pay for the infrastructure and
community impacts
associated with data center growth.
Salinas said that the bill is intended to ensure communities are not left bearing the costs of rising data center demand and share in the benefits generated by that growth. “Every community deserves to drive a hard bargain with data center developers, and at the end of the day, every community deserves to share in the benefits from data center growth,” she said in a press statement.
Related:
Nebraska Reins in Data Center Perks Amid Resource Scrutiny
The proposal would build on a state-level approach that
Virginia adopted
earlier this year. Virginia became the first state to impose a tax directly on data center electricity consumption, setting the rate at 1.1 cents per kilowatt-hour beginning July 1 and applying it to electricity supplied by utilities and retail providers as well as self-generated power, including
behind-the-meter generation
. State budget documents projected about $600 million in annual revenue for the general fund.
The federal bill would set a slightly lower rate but apply it nationwide. Unlike Virginia’s tax, however, Salinas’ proposal would allocate the revenue among five federal funds rather than sending it to a general fund.
What Operators Would Pay at Scale
Neil Osnato, founder of Persistence Analytics Group, said the tax could be significant for large data center operators, but its broader implications depend on whether electricity consumption is an appropriate proxy for the costs individual facilities impose on the grid.
At continuous full load, a 100 MW data center would incur about $8.76 million annually under the tax; at 500 MW, about $43.8 million; and at 1 GW, about $87.6 million. At a 90% annual load factor (actual average usage as a percentage of maximum), those figures would be approximately $7.9 million, $39.4 million, and $78.8 million, respectively.
Related:
Data Centers’ Next Hurdle: Winning Public Trust and Social License
The tax could affect data center siting and power procurement at the margin, particularly when operators compare jurisdictions with otherwise similar power economics, Osnato said. For the largest AI and hyperscale projects, however, access to executable megawatts, transmission availability, interconnection timing, generation supply, and development certainty may matter more than the tax alone.
If a facility’s underlying electricity price were 5¢/kWh, the proposed tax would add 20% to the energy component. At 10¢/kWh, it would add 10%, Osnato said.
The bill defines a data center as a facility that primarily contains electronic equipment used to process, store, or transmit digital information and has a maximum rated power capacity or total peak power load exceeding 1 MW.
Flat Tax vs. Grid Cost Causation
Osnato said the proposal should not be confused with a mechanism for assigning electricity system costs to the customers that cause them.
“The bigger issue is cost causation,” Osnato said.
Two 500 MW data centers could consume the same amount of electricity while imposing very different costs on the grid, depending on where they locate, how their demand coincides with system peaks, what transmission and substation upgrades they require, whether new generation must be procured, and how flexible their operations are, he said.
Related:
Texas’ 765 kV Decision: Build the Wires, the AI Will Follow
“A flat federal consumption tax does not distinguish among any of those conditions,” Osnato said.
Data centers already pay through multiple layers of the electricity system, including energy, transmission, distribution, and capacity costs, as well as
customer-specific interconnection or construction charges
in some cases. The policy question, Osnato said, is whether existing mechanisms fully capture the electrical consequences of new large loads.
“A federal tax does not substitute for that analysis,” he added.
Revenue Split: Five Federal Funds
The legislation would distribute amounts equivalent to one-fifth of annual receipts to each of five destinations:
The Land and Water Conservation Fund
The Housing Trust Fund
The Hazardous Substance Superfund
The Highway Trust Fund
A new Energy Technology Trust Fund established by the bill
Salinas’ office projects about $1.76 billion in annual revenue based on current nationwide data center electricity use, allocating roughly $352 million per year for each of the five funds. The release says the Energy Technology Trust Fund would support federal loan guarantees for clean energy, advanced nuclear, and grid infrastructure projects.
People’s Counsel David S. Lapp said the proposed tax could increase federal revenue for programs that benefit the public but does little to address the way data center growth is affecting electricity costs for existing customers.
“Those risks arise largely from existing PJM rules for the administration of its capacity market and transmission planning that, without necessary reforms, will force residential customers to subsidize massive data center growth,” Lapp told Data Center Knowledge.
Lapp said ratepayer protections need to address capacity and energy costs, transmission costs and distribution costs. He said those measures should include requiring data center customers to bring their own generation or accept curtailment, reforming PJM’s rules for assigning data center-driven transmission costs, and implementing large-load tariffs with stronger protections.
Tax Would Apply Broadly
The bill does not specify a separate rate for AI data centers. Instead, the tax would apply based on electricity consumption by facilities meeting the bill’s 1 MW threshold.
That threshold means the proposal reaches well beyond the largest hyperscale AI campuses. It could also apply to smaller colocation, enterprise, and institutional data centers with more than 1 MW of maximum rated capacity or peak load.
The legislation also covers electricity generated onsite, according to Salinas’ office.
Osnato said policymakers should distinguish between electricity consumption and its consequences for the grid.
“The questions that matter are: Is the projected load real? When will it actually materialize? How durable will it be? What generation, transmission, and local infrastructure does it cause?” Osnato said.
He also said policymakers should determine which costs are customer-specific versus genuinely regional and whether a facility’s operating characteristics increase or reduce system burden.
“Megawatts are not interchangeable,” Osnato said.
Tax Revenue Doesn’t Assign Actual Grid Costs
Osnato said customer-specific costs should follow the customer that causes them, while genuinely shared system costs should be shared to the extent that the benefits are systemwide. The bill instead uses electricity consumption as a proxy for the costs and impacts associated with data center growth, while directing the revenue to five federal programs that are not specifically tied to the electricity infrastructure serving the facilities.
Only the proposed Energy Technology Trust Fund has a direct energy connection, and its proceeds would support federal loan guarantees rather than specifically funding the local or regional grid infrastructure created by the taxed facility.
“Policymakers could collect money from the right industry while still allocating the underlying grid costs incorrectly,” Osnato said.
If enacted, the bill’s amendments would apply to electricity used and taxes received after the date of enactment.
The proposal remains at the introduced stage after its Aug. 13 referral to the three House committees.

title: Nvidia Backs OpenAI’s Ohio Data Center Buildout With $105B
content:
Nvidia is putting up as much as $105 billion in residual-value guarantees for OpenAI’s planned Ohio data center campus, giving the chipmaker a financial role in the AI infrastructure buildout that goes beyond supplying GPUs.
The guarantees cover an initial 4.25 GW of IT capacity at SB Energy’s PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio. Nvidia also has an option to provide support for another 3.75 GW, bringing the planned campus to about 8 GW of IT capacity. SB Energy will build, own and operate the campus under a 20-year lease with
Nvidia disclosed the guarantees in an August 17
SEC filing
. Its aggregate payment obligation for the initial guarantees is capped at $105 billion. The guarantees are tied to the residual value of the leased infrastructure rather than representing a $105 billion investment in the project.
If specified default or insolvency events occur, Nvidia may be responsible for a shortfall between the guaranteed minimum value under the leases and the amounts recovered by SB Energy through re-leasing or selling the facilities. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify Nvidia for amounts Nvidia actually pays under the guarantees.
Related:
APAC Data Center Pipeline Surges as AI Pre-Leasing Tightens Supply
The actual guarantee agreements have not yet been filed. Nvidia said it will include the exhibits in its quarterly report for the period ended July 26, which will provide the detailed terms and guaranteed minimum values.
Leveraging the GPU as an Investable Asset Class
Nvidia is describing the Ohio data center project in terms that emphasize the long useful life of the infrastructure.
“We are securing long-lived infrastructure for Nvidia compute so OpenAI can deploy the most productive
AI factories
that can be upgraded repeatedly with each new generation delivering more intelligence and better economics,” CEO Jensen Huang said in Nvidia’s announcement.
Steven Dickens, CEO and principal analyst at HyperFrame Research, said Nvidia appears to be recognizing that GPUs retain value after their initial deployment.
“NVIDIA is realizing, in the same way that Ford Finance does with Ford’s vehicles, that GPUs have a residual value long after the initial three years of use,” Dickens said.
Dickens said Nvidia can use that residual value to create an investable asset class and bring additional capital into the AI infrastructure buildout.
“Leveraging the GPU as an investable asset class is a smart move by Nvidia as it unlocks capital for the AI build-out,” he said.
AI hardware can have useful lives of six to seven years or longer, Dickens said, creating room for financing models that account for value remaining after an initial deployment.
Related:
Galaxy Bets Its Data Center Edge on Power, Not ‘Bragawatts’
The Ohio arrangement connects three pieces of the AI infrastructure stack: Nvidia’s hardware, OpenAI’s long-term demand for compute, and SB Energy’s ownership of the physical data center.
Conditional Guarantee
The $105 billion figure needs to be separated from the amount Nvidia is actually investing.
Nvidia is investing $1.5 billion in SB Energy, while the guarantee is a separate contractual commitment tied to the initial 4.25 GW deployment. Nvidia says it has secured land, power and shell capacity at the site and will be the exclusive AI compute infrastructure provider.
The guarantee is conditional. It does not mean Nvidia has committed $105 billion of cash to build the Ohio campus.
Instead, the residual-value guarantees provide credit support tied to the leased facilities. The 8-K says Nvidia’s obligations can be triggered by specified events involving OpenAI and the leases, with the payment obligation based on the difference between guaranteed minimum values and amounts recovered by SB Energy.
The structure leaves an important question for the next filing: how much
financing
capacity does the residual-value guarantee actually create? The forthcoming guarantee agreements should provide the answer.
Related:
CoreWeave Enters APAC Data Center Race With Indonesia Expansion
Power is Not Compute
Dickens also questioned the industry’s
growing reliance on power capacity
as the primary metric for describing AI infrastructure.
“What I struggle with is measuring the AI build-out in units of power,” he said. “I would prefer Nvidia and the wider IT infrastructure business stick to IT units such as core, GPU, racks or servers, as it is easier to quantify and visualize.”
The initial OpenAI deployment at the Ohio campus is expected to provide 4.25 GW of IT capacity, with another 3.75 GW potentially bringing the campus to about 8 GW. SB Energy and SoftBank have separately said they plan to develop at least 10 GW of new energy generation to support the project.

title: Ausgrid in Australia begins construction on 400 MWh BESS, scores approval for another 400 MWh - Energy Storage
content: Australian distribution network operator, Ausgrid, along with Plus Grid Storage, a separate commercial entity that will build and operate the project, has begun construction on the 200 MW / 400 MWh Steel River East battery energy storage system (BESS) in Newcastle, New South Wales, some 200 kilometers north of Sydney. The project is located at the Steel River Industrial Estate in the city of Newcastle, and will consist of 112 Tesla Megapack 2XL lithium-ion battery units. It will connect to Ausgrid’s 132 kV zone substation via a 33 kV underground cable. Construction approval was granted in March 2026 by the NSW Independent Planning Commission (IPC). It was initially referred to the IPC due to 61 public objections being made to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) during the assessment period. Plus Grid Storage is a partnership between the NSW government, IFM investors, APG Group, and AustralianSuper. The company announced the start of construction on LinkedIn. “This is an exciting step forward for PLUS Grid Storage as we move into delivery on our first project, reflecting the hard work of our team, project partners and stakeholders. Steel River East BESS will play an important role in supporting a more reliable and resilient electricity network by storing excess energy when demand is low and dispatching it back to the grid when it is needed most,” the post said. The Steel River East BESS is expected to be operational by late 2027. Homebush BESS secures planning approval Ausgrid’s 200 MW / 400 MWh Homebush BESS , to also be developed by Plus Grid Storage, secured planning approval earlier in the month. The project is located 15 kilometers west of Sydney’s CBD in New South Wales. It will be adjacent to the existing 132 kV Mason Park sub-transmission switching station. Homebush will also be using the same Tesla Megapack 2XL units as Steel River East. “We’re proud to be progressing a pipeline of strategically located storage projects that will strengthen the electricity network and support homes, businesses and communities across NSW,” said Kelly Wood, Ausgrid executive in charge of Plus Grid Storage. Plus Grid Storage said that “an additional six projects are progressing through the NSW planning system.” Once complete, the company will have around 1 GW of battery storage capacity, with a 2031 target being set. title: Blocked BESS in Britain: Clearstone's appeal fails for 150 MW site at Axminster [UPDATED] - Energy Storage
content: Clearstone Energy’s Axminster Energy Hub, set to be a 150 MW battery energy storage system (BESS), has had its appeal rejected by the planning inspector appointed by the Secretary of State. Clearstone Energy (Clearstone) had announced the project in 2023, following its receipt of a grid connection at National Grid’s Axminster Substation, located 4 km to the east of Axminster, near the border of Devon and Dorset in England. It applied for a permit to East Devon District Council (EDDC) in early 2024 under application 24/0096/MFUL, which was rejected by the Council in May 2025. At the council’s 3.5-hour-long hearing, there was significant local pushback against the potential for fires and concerns about pollution of local water sources. Clearstone appealed, though the EDDC withdrew its opposition during the appeal process following a meeting on January 14, 2026. That left the opposition to local groups dubbed a “Rule 6 Party,” which continued to oppose the appeal. Local groups have fought against several BESS projects in the area, raising considerable funds to support fielding expert advice at hearings. Following a hearing and lengthy decision process, planning inspector Helen Heward dismissed the appeal on August 13, 2026, in a 17-page decision. In the statement, which accounts for all preliminary matters, two “Main Issues” were noted. “ i) The risk of a fire event and whether, in the event of a fire, the proposed fire safety and pollution control measures would be sufficient to prevent pollution of aquifers and control the quality of groundwater, with particular regard to the health and safety of local residents. “ ii) The effect of the proposal upon the character and appearance of the local area including the Dorset National Landscape. “ In the latter issue, detailed discussions of the BESS’s “alien” appearance were mentioned in the context of the natural landscape. More than a dozen points on this matter were made. The discussion of fire risk, however, was far more substantial. Risk of fires Clearstone nominated the Wärtsilä Quantum 1 BESS, a lithium iron phosphate battery type, for the site. 52 units were scheduled for installation. In the decision, the Wärtsilä Quantum 1 BESS system was noted as being installed at 100 sites worldwide and 9 sites in the UK, including the UK’s largest BESS facility at Blackhillock in Scotland . It was noted as meeting regulations, including “NFPA 855 minimum standards for BESS hazard mitigation, NFPA 69 Standard on Explosion Prevention Systems, and NFPA 68 standard on Explosion Protection by Deflagration Venting”, and the large-scale first test (LSFT) for the Quantum 1 was examined in the hearing. It was noted that the technology had a 100% safety track record. Fire experts represented both sides of the appeal, with Martin Blunden acting as an expert for Clearstone Energy, a “Member of the Institute of Fire Engineers, a former Chief Fire Officer of the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service with extensive experience in the UK Fire and Rescue sector, including roles for the National Fire Chiefs Council on Health and Safety.” Acting for the Rule 6 Party, Jeremy Ramsden accepted that, based on 2025 failure rates, there was a 99.76% chance of no fire in any given year. Over the site’s planned 40-year lifetime, Ramsden provided standard calculations indicating an approximate 10% probability of at least one fire. Developers typically question this logic with caveats that batteries are monitored, and typically augmented or replaced during a project lifetime as they degrade. The decision notes that replacements would happen at around 15 years. Typically, engineers also point to bathtub curves that dictate failure rates versus a single static number, though the planning inspector notes there is not one industry-agreed model. Also used as evidence were reports from Clean Energy Associates , which found that “26% of BESS units inspected had defects in the fire suppression system, 18% had thermal management system defects, and system-level defects accounted for nearly 50% of all quality assurance findings.” Decision The planning inspector noted, “I am not persuaded that there is sufficient robust evidence to demonstrate that the deflagration/explosion mitigation strategies would work effectively and that explosion hazards would be satisfactorily controlled for cabinets 10cm apart.” Heward continued, “Whilst the issue may be finely balanced, as a matter of fire safety, this weighs very heavily against the proposal. And, as the evidence for pollution control is predicated on the fire safety evidence, it follows that I cannot be confident that pollution control measures, such as the extent and size of the fire water retention blanket, would be sufficient to prevent pollution of aquifers and control the quality of groundwater.” ESS News contacted Clearstone for comment, and Rob Garratt, head of development, Clearstone Energy, sent the following statement. This is a deeply concerning decision for anyone with BESS projects in the UK and for a Government that has worked hard to reassure that the right processes and guidelines are in place to ensure that the 25GW increase in BESS in its Clean Power Plan requirements can be delivered safely. The NFCC guidance was followed to the letter with a comprehensive pre-application consultation with DSFRS and a proposal that went above and beyond the NFCC Guidance in place when the planning application was submitted (2023) and therefore met the 2026 update to the guidance . A BESS manufacturer, Wärtsilä, was specified within the planning application. The system is proven in the field, maintains a 100% safety record, and has successfully passed all safety tests, including the Large Scale Fire Test, which is now part of UL9450A and therefore the latest NFCC guidance. East Devon District Council decided not to defend the appeal following expert review of the proposal. This decision effectively says to Councils that being compliant with the NFCC guidance isn’t enough to demonstrate that safety has been satisfactorily addressed. It risks undoing all the good work that has been done by manufacturers, the fire service and Government to ensure and assure that UK BESS schemes will operate safely. Clearstone Energy maintains that this is a well-designed and much-needed project to support the UK’s Clean Power ambitions. We are reviewing the options available to us to challenge this decision for this project, but also the wider industry. title: Czechia's largest BESS goes online - Energy Storage
content: Czech industrial holding Suas Group and Slovak investment firm EIF have energized a 57 MW / 120 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in near the town of Lipnice nad Sázavou, located in Czechia’s Vysočina Region, some 100 kilometers southeast of Prague. The 400 million CZK (USD 19.1 million) Lipnice BESS is now the largest operational battery storage system in Czechia. The second-largest is the 37.95 MW/41.7 MWh BESS at the Modlany Energy Park in northern Czechia , which was commissioned earlier this month. The two companies said the facility can be used to help maintain the stability of the Czech electricity system, provide ancillary services to Czech transmission system operator ČEPS, or participate in commercial arbitrage on the day-ahead and intraday electricity markets. The facility comprises 144 battery cabinets, 18 power conversion systems, and nine transformer skids. “The storage facility could supply electricity to a city the size of nearby Sokolov for ten hours,” the joint statement reads. “It is a key tool for optimizing electricity trading and managing imbalances effectively.” “It makes no sense to base the battery economy solely on providing technical flexibility,” the two companies went on to say. “Therefore, we will use BESS Lipnice primarily on the daily and intraday market.” Suas Group believes BESS Lipnice will pay for itself within five to eight years, supported by revenues from multiple electricity markets and smart algorithmic management. The future of the Czech Republic’s energy storage market will be driven by utility-scale investments and favorable regulations, according to analysis by Aurora Energy Research from November 2025. The agency forecasted the country’s total battery storage capacity to hit 6 GWh by the end of the decade. title: Germany's Bayernwerk changes grid connection criteria for BESS, and consumers - Energy Storage
content: First come, first served no longer. This principle is now finished with at Germany’s Bayernwerk Netz—the major distribution system operator (DSO) serving the German state of Bavaria and a subsidiary of energy giant E.ON. The change applies specifically to battery storage systems with more than 300 kW of import capacity and consumers with a power requirement exceeding 1,000 kW. Moving forward, an allocation procedure based on published criteria will apply to these grid connections. With this change, the distribution grid operator aims to allocate available grid capacity in a more transparent, predictable, and efficient manner. Netze BW, another major grid operator in the neighboring state of Baden-Württemberg, home of the Black Forest, also recently moved away from the first-come, first-served approach. In the future, project maturity will be the primary deciding factor for grid connections there. Unlike Bayernwerk Netz, however, the Netze BW procedure also applies to generating facilities with a capacity of 950 kW or more. Willingness to provide flexibility taken into account When allocating capacity, Bayernwerk Netz will weigh criteria including a project’s maturity, willingness to provide flexibility, potential for co-location with a renewable energy plant, consideration of local infrastructure, and location constraints resulting from investments already made. The grid operator will also factor in the project’s contribution to statutory climate targets. Bayernwerk Netz will collect all applications in semi-annual cycles and prioritize them based on these defined criteria. The technical grid assessment will then follow this prioritization. The allocation process ends when the available grid connection capacity has been distributed or the priority list of eligible applications has been fully processed. The grid operator intends to prevent speculative applications by requiring a realization deposit, stressing that capacity requests should only be submitted for seriously planned projects. After the procedure is completed, all applicants will receive binding feedback on whether they were allocated capacity. Projects that are not selected can participate again in the next allocation cycle, though application data will not be carried over automatically. Exemptions The criteria-based allocation procedure is effective immediately, with the digital application portal scheduled to launch on October 12, 2026. Exempt from the new procedure are generators as well as vulnerable institutions such as hospitals, emergency services, and educational facilities. The new process also does not apply to so-called green power storage systems, as they do not draw power from the distribution grid. Heating projects based on municipal heat planning are similarly exempt. For all these groups, the existing connection process remains unchanged. As the new allocation procedure does not inherently create additional grid capacity, the Bayernwerk subsidiary plans to invest around €12 billion in grid expansion between 2026 and 2030. title: Origin begins commercial operations at 650 MWh Mortlake grid-forming BESS in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Australian energy company Origin Energy has announced the commencement of commercial operations at the 300 MW / 650 MWh Mortlake battery energy storage system (BESS) in south-west Victoria. Located around 220 kilometers west of the Melbourne CBD, the Mortlake BESS is built right next to Origin Energy’s existing Mortlake Power Station. Grid connection is delivered through a dedicated substation linked into AusNet’s 500 kV Mortlake switchyard. The system is designated MLB01 in the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) registry. Construction of the Mortlake BESS began in August 2024 after first being announced in January 2024 with an investment of approximately AU$400 million. US-based energy storage specialist Fluence served as the EPC contractor and grid-forming inverters were sourced from German manufacturer SMA. The grid-forming inverters differ from traditional inverters with technology and hardware designed to support the grid when required, rather than simply following it. In the above image which takes AEMO data, MLB01 can be seen operating via charging/discharging onto the grid. title: Ex-Tesla president: Roadster delay is about getting closer to SpaceX ahead of merger
content:
Tesla Roadster
New Tesla Roadster
Fred Lambert
| Aug 19 2026 - 6:40 am PT
A former Tesla president says the endlessly delayed next-generation Roadster is being held up by SpaceX “hovering” technology — and that the project is really about pulling Tesla and SpaceX closer together.
Jon McNeill, Tesla’s president from 2015 to 2018 and now co-founder of VistaShares and CEO of DVx Ventures, made the comments as Tesla preps a long-promised Roadster demo nearly nine years after the car was first unveiled.
What the ex-president said
Speaking about the upcoming demonstration, McNeill said the event could show off the car’s most extreme party trick.
“I don’t know if we’re going to see flying, but we may see hovering in this demo,” he said via
McNeill framed the Roadster as a morale play for a company under pressure. “Elon recognizes that Tesla needs to inject some energy and excitement back into the car business,” he said.
He was more direct about the strategic motive. McNeill called the Roadster a “probably not-so-hidden attempt to further knit Tesla and SpaceX’s futures together,” and predicted the two companies “are going to come together, probably sooner rather than later.”
The “hovering” comes from a SpaceX-developed cold-gas thruster system, internally code-named A71, that points toward the ground to lift the car. We reported last week that Tesla’s
“flying” Roadster demo could happen this month
— and that the car would be remotely operated with no one inside, in part because the thrusters are loud enough to damage the hearing of anyone nearby.
A car promised in 2017 — and delayed at least nine times
Tesla unveiled the new Roadster in November 2017 with production promised for 2020. The reservation program asked buyers to put down up to $50,000, and Founders Series buyers wired the full $250,000.
The original specs were: a claimed 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds, a top speed above 250 mph, and a 620-mile range — numbers that made it, on paper, the quickest production car ever announced. None of it required rocket thrusters.
The SpaceX package came later, as an add-on Elon Musk teased would cut the 0-60 time to roughly 1.1 seconds using cold-gas thrusters. Since then, the car has been
delayed at least nine times
. The demo alone has slipped from April 1, 2026, to late April, to “maybe in a month” on the Q1 earnings call, to August 2026 — and now the thruster work is the reason it isn’t ready.
Even the demo has been scaled back. Earlier plans reportedly had the car racing up a magnetized ramp, driving upside down, righting itself, and hovering. Those elements were cut after being presented to Musk, who said about the demo “will be hard to pull off and could go wrong, but that it will be entertaining either way.”
The financial backdrop
The timing matters. TSLA is down roughly 25% year-to-date, the worst performer among the “Magnificent Seven,” and Tesla’s core auto business has been shrinking as competition intensifies. The full history of the program is tracked in our
Tesla Roadster guide
McNeill’s read that the Roadster is meant to “inject some energy and excitement” and knit Tesla and SpaceX together lands against that backdrop of a struggling car business and open speculation about a Tesla-SpaceX combination.
Electrek’s Take
Let’s be clear about what this is: a demo. That’s likely all it’s going to be.
It may well be true that the SpaceX cold-air thruster work is what’s holding up the Roadster, but if that’s the case, it’s bad business. The Roadster Tesla unveiled in 2017 was extremely well received. It didn’t have thrusters from SpaceX, and it didn’t need them. A 1.9-second 0-60, 250-plus mph, and a 620-mile range was already the most exciting car anyone had announced. No one who put down $50,000 was asking for cold-gas rockets that make the car undriveable and un-street-legal. Nobody is asking for that.
Tesla should just deliver the car it showed nearly nine years ago – hopefully with some upgrades since it has been a decade. Instead, the company is bolting on a gimmick with almost no real-world utility so it can stage a driverless “hovering” stunt in a Texas field.
And McNeill might be right about tying Tesla and SpaceX closer together ahead of a potential merger that would primarily benefit a single shareholder. Using a highly anticipated, long-overdue product as a prop for that agenda, when you had a great car to begin with, is pathetic. Deliver the Roadster people actually paid for, and do it 8 years ago. The rocket show can wait, and you don’t even need it. Elon can force anything he wants on Tesla shareholders and they will say thank you. History has proven that time and time again.

title: Here's our first look at the new Hyundai Tucson inside and out [Images]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 19 2026 - 7:55 am PT
revealed the exterior and interior design of the all-new Tucson for the first time, and it already looks like a big upgrade.
Meet the new Hyundai Tucson
It’s been six years since Hyundai launched the current fourth-generation Tucson. For the fifth-gen model, Hyundai is taking the SUV to the next level.
The new Hyundai Tucson has grown up and now looks more like a traditional SUV, with a wide, boxy stance.
The new look is based on Hyundai’s “Art of Steel” design, the same design philosophy behind the off-road Boulder Concept from the New York Auto Show earlier this year.
Hyundai’s bold off-road-like design is becoming its signature, similar to the new look that Kia has created over the past few years.
Up front, the redesigned Tucson features new vertical “H-edge” daytime running lights and a slim horizontal light bar. Hyundai said the lights in the bar are not directly exposed on the outside, helping to create the bold, three-dimensional look.
The new Hyundai Tucson (Source: Hyundai)
The rear features a prism rear lamp with a three-dimensional protruding lens structure. When illuminated, the lamp is revealed, adding “visual three-dimensionality.”
The new Hyundai Tucson measures 4,700 mm (185″) long, 1,905 mm (75″) wide, and 1,685 mm (66″) high, with a 2,785 mm (110″) wheelbase.
The new Hyundai Tucson (Source: Hyundai)
Compared to the current model, the new Tucson is 60 mm longer, 40 mm wider, and has a 40 mm longer wheelbase. The increased dimensions open up “best-in-class interior space,” according to Hyundai.
The interior is fully redesigned, with a new floating structure to open up space and a large center infotainment screen.
New Hyundai Tucson interior (Source: Hyundai)
Hyundai equipped the new Tucson with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system. The setup includes a large center display with apps and customizable screens, plus a slim driver display.
The new Tucson will be available with Hyundai’s XRT trim, which adds to the rugged, off-road design. Added design elements include an exclusive front grille, wheels, and skid plates, black wheel arch garnishes, and XRT badging.
The new Hyundai Tucson and Tucson XRT (Source: Hyundai)
Inside, the Tucson XRT features exclusive patterned seats, dark metal decor, and protective floor mats for the first and second rows.
Hyundai has yet to reveal powertrain details, but like the current Tucson, the new version is expected to be sold as a hybrid and plug-in hybrid, not pure electric.
While the Tucson likely won’t be offered with a fully electric powertrain, Hyundai still offers the
, which is about the same size. We will have to wait until closer to launch for the full details.

title: Lucid unveils its 2027 Air EV lineup with a new Stealth package
content:
Lucid unveiled its 2027 Air lineup, streamlining the options across its electric sedan range and adding a new Stealth & Sound Package for the entry-level Air Pure.
The Air Grand Touring keeps its title as the longest-range EV on sale at up to 512 miles, and pricing holds flat across all four trims for the new model year.
What’s new for 2027
The biggest change is in the configurator, not the car. Lucid says the 2027 pricing guides “reflect a more focused set of available options for Air Pure,” trimming the entry model’s long à la carte menu down to a tighter set of choices.
The centerpiece is a new Stealth & Sound Package for the Air Pure, priced at $6,250, that bundles the most popular options into a single configuration. Buyers who add it can pick either 19-inch Aero Range Stealth or 20-inch Aero Lite Stealth wheels, plus a paint finish in Infinite Black Metallic, Stellar White Metallic, or Quantum Grey Metallic.
The Touring, Grand Touring, and Sapphire carry into 2027 largely as they were. The whole lineup is configurable now through Lucid’s Design Yours tool.
Prices hold flat across the lineup
Every trim keeps its 2026 starting price for the new model year, in both the US and Canada. That’s worth a note in 2026: tariffs on imported vehicles and parts have pushed costs up across the industry, and the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired at the end of September 2025, so effective EV prices have been climbing. Lucid left the Air’s sticker alone.
Top comment by Beario
While I like Lucid and wish them success, this year and early next year will be important for them with the release of the Gravity model. Not taking anything away from an updated Air, but it would have been great if Lucid had laid out a roadmap filled with more vehicles like Rivian did when they introduced the R2, R3, and R3X but even one more Lucid model gives hope that they can last and be profitable to build more cars down the road.
Here’s the lineup, 2026 versus 2027:
| Air | 2026 US | 2027 US | 2026 Canada | 2027 Canada | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pure | $70,900 | $70,900 | CA$99,900 | CA$99,900 | No change |
| Touring | $79,900 | $79,900 | CA$112,800 | CA$112,800 | No change |
| Grand Touring | $114,900 | $114,900 | CA$161,200 | CA$161,200 | No change |
| Sapphire | $249,000 | $249,000 | CA$327,300 | CA$327,300 | No change |
It helps that the Air is selling well at the top of its class. We reported last year that the Air became the best-selling luxury EV sedan in the US, passing Tesla’s Model S. And the range crown isn’t just an EPA number — the Air won Norway’s brutal EV winter test earlier this year, a real-world result that’s harder to argue with than a lab figure.
However, the focus for Lucid has been on the Gravity this year and it is showing in this lack of change with the 2027 model year.

title: VMAX VX2 Lite review: Power and full suspension fun without the heavyweight price
content:
electric scooter
Micah Toll
| Aug 19 2026 - 7:35 am PT
Electric scooters have long demonstrated an interesting dichotomy. On one end of the spectrum, you’ve got cheap commuter scooters that feel like they’re one pothole away from shaking themselves apart. On the other end are increasingly large, dual-motor monsters that weigh 80 or 100 pounds (45 kg) and blur the line between scooter and motorcycle.
The VMAX VX2 Lite aims for the sweet spot in the middle. It promises a genuine full-suspension ride, respectable 25 mph (40 km/h) performance, and up to 56 miles (90 km) of claimed range without turning into something you dread carrying up a flight of stairs. After spending time riding the long-range version, I think VMAX got surprisingly close to that goal.
I’ll tell you all about my experience riding the VMAX VX2 Lite electric scooter below, but why not also see it in action? Check out my review video here, then keep reading for all of my complete thoughts.
Suspension is the real star of the show
The biggest selling point here is undoubtedly the suspension.
The VX2 Lite combines a 47 mm hydraulic front fork with an elastomer rear suspension, and while that spec sheet doesn’t sound particularly exciting, it completely changes how the scooter feels to ride.
Instead of constantly bracing for cracks in the pavement or rough patches of asphalt, you simply ride through them. Expansion joints, brick streets, uneven bike paths, and rough pavement all become significantly less jarring.
And while the scooter is definitely not an off-roader, I specifically took it through some grass and dirt sections just to see how it fared. The street tires aren’t really optimized for it, but the scooter handled dry off-road sections just fine.
More importantly, that suspension doesn’t just make a scooter more comfortable – it makes it more fun. There’s a weird child-like thrill from purposefully ramping off of speed bumps when you know the landing is going to be controlled and not shake your ankle bones out of position.
I found myself taking routes I might normally avoid simply because the scooter handled rough surfaces so much better. The tires stay planted, the steering feels calmer, and the overall ride inspires more confidence. It transforms the experience from cautiously avoiding imperfections to simply enjoying the ride.
That’s a hard thing to appreciate from a spec sheet, but it’s immediately obvious once you’re rolling.
Surprisingly punchy performance
The other pleasant surprise was the motor.
On paper, the VX2 Lite uses a 500W nominal rear hub motor with up to 1,400W peak output. The continuous power number off 500W doesn’t necessarily scream performance, but the scooter feels much stronger than I expected. That’s the peak power speaking. And to really make use of that peak power, you’ll want to put the scooter in Beast Mode (five quick pushes on the power button and then one push of the throttle). For some people, that may even be more power than they need, but if you can handle it, it’s a lot of fun to have that much acceleration underneath you.
Don’t worry though, if you just leave it in normal mode then you’re still getting a lot of the scooter, plus you’ll have the benefit of even longer range – but more on that soon.
Acceleration is brisk enough to keep city riding entertaining, and I never found myself wishing for significantly more power during normal urban riding. I don’t have a ton of hills to test out in my flat city, but climbing parking garage ramps and other short steep ramps definitely showed off the power hiding away in this scooter. VMAX’s claimed ability to climb grades up to 28% isn’t something I could test myself (most people don’t have any 28% grade hills in their area – that’s some serious incline), but it also doesn’t seem unrealistic for shorter climbs, based on what I experienced.
The 25 mph (40 km/h) top speed also feels like a nice balance. It’s quick enough to comfortably keep pace with urban traffic in many situations without venturing into the “this is getting a little ridiculous” territory occupied by some high-performance scooters.
Even on the crazy super scooters that can hit twice these speeds or more, I rarely like going much faster than 40 mph (64 km/h), and even that feels a bit reckless unless the wheels are huge. Here, 25 mph (40 km/h) seems sensibly fast, especially since people rarely use the absolute top speed of a scooter anyway. And with 10″ tires, these are actually larger wheels than you’ll find on a lot of budget scooters, so you have a bit more confidence at these speeds, too.
A commuter that feels well thought out
Little design decisions often separate good scooters from great ones, and VMAX deserves credit for getting a lot of those details right.
One of my favorites is the folding latch. After unfolding the scooter, the latch folds neatly down against the deck and locks itself out of the way. It sounds like a tiny feature, but anyone who’s ever had a folding latch poking into their foot while riding will immediately appreciate it.
I saw it on the VX2 Hub also
, a faster and more powerful big brother to the VX2 Lite, and it’s a neat little feature.
The folding mechanism in the stem also feels reassuringly solid. There’s no discernible play once locked into position, giving the scooter a sturdy, confidence-inspiring feel.
VMAX has long made good lighting a priority on its electric scooters, complete with deck and bar-mounted turn signals
Lighting is another highlight.
The VX2 Lite doesn’t settle for a basic headlight and tiny rear reflector. Instead, it includes bright lighting all around, complete with motorcycle-style turn signals integrated into both the deck and the ends of the handlebars. They’re much more visible than the tiny blinking indicators found on many scooters, and anything that makes riders more noticeable to drivers gets a thumbs-up from me.
Again, this is par for the course with VMAX, as I’ve enjoyed this well-designed wraparound lighting with highly visible turn signals
on several of the company’s models before
. It’s an important part of riding, especially at night when you’re basically just a narrow vertical stick on two wheels, compared to cars looking for other cars.
Thank you for not forcing an app
This is becoming one of my biggest pet peeves in the micromobility industry.
Too many companies now expect riders to download an app, create an account, pair the scooter, verify an email address, and usually even accept privacy policies before they can access basic functions.
Thankfully, VMAX didn’t go down that road.
The companion app exists if you want additional ride data and customization, but you don’t need it.
Power modes, riding settings, and normal operation can all be handled directly from the scooter itself. And to prevent having too many buttons, several features (like opening and locking that Beast Mode) are performed by the same button, just with different numbers of quick presses.
Not requiring an app might sound like a small thing, but I genuinely appreciate products that still function perfectly well without requiring me to download another app onto my phone.
It’s just how these vehicles should work.
Weight and value
At around 52 lb (23.6 kg) for the larger battery version I tested, or 48 lb (21.8 kg) for the smaller battery version, I wouldn’t call the VX2 Lite lightweight. You’ll still notice it if you’re carrying it upstairs every day.
But context matters here. Compared to many other full-suspension scooters with similar ride quality and performance, it’s actually fairly light. VMAX has done a nice job balancing portability with comfort, and I think they landed in a reasonable place.
Pricing is another pleasant surprise.
The lineup starts at
$799 for the 499 Wh version
with a claimed 31-mile range, while the larger 874 Wh battery model I tested
comes in at $1,099
. In today’s market, that’s a pretty competitive starting price for a scooter that delivers this level of refinement, suspension, and performance.
Sure, there are cheaper models from a never-ending list of Chinese companies, and I’m not knocking them, but you do feel a real difference in the quality and ride of a VMAX scooter. So in this case, you get what you pay for – and I still think the price is fair. Add in the included 2-year warranty, which twice what the budget brands usually offer, and it looks even better.
And with reasonable pricing, you get to save some cash for extra accessories. I tested out the folding lock from VMAX, and it’s a convenient way to carry a small lock in a holster on the scooter itself, but that still opens up into a large circle for locking to non-standard racks, small trees, etc. But they’ve got tons of
other accessories
worth checking out, also.
A couple of things I’d still change
No product is perfect, and the VX2 Lite isn’t an exception.
My biggest complaint is simply that I’d always prefer a scooter to weigh less. While it’s lighter than many competitors in this category, 50-ish pounds is still enough that you’ll think twice before carrying it long distances.
The other nitpick is cosmetic.
The available colorway is clean and understated, but it doesn’t exactly stand out. To be fair, most electric scooter manufacturers seem convinced that buyers only want black scooters, so VMAX isn’t exactly alone here. Still, a splash of color would have been nice. But then again, a black canvas does give you plenty of open real estate to play around with your own coloring, stickers, or however you want to customize your ride.
Final thoughts
The VMAX VX2 Lite manages to do something I always appreciate: it avoids chasing spec-sheet bragging rights and instead focuses on making the riding experience better.
The suspension genuinely improves both comfort and fun. The motor feels stronger than its rating suggests. The thoughtful design touches make everyday use easier. And perhaps most refreshing of all, it works perfectly well without demanding you install another smartphone app just to ride it.
If you’re shopping for a commuter scooter in the $800-$1,100 range and your priorities are ride quality, comfort, visibility, and solid real-world performance rather than outrageous top speeds, the VX2 Lite deserves a spot near the top of your list.
Sometimes, making a scooter more enjoyable isn’t about adding another motor or another 10 mph. Sometimes it’s simply about making every mile feel smoother and
. The VX2 Lite is a great example of exactly that.

title: 晶科/弘元/华晟/尚德获海内外光伏组件订单
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，光伏组件订单及项目持续落地。晶科能源、弘元绿能、华晟新能源、尚德相继推进国内外项目及订单，覆盖集中式、工商业及海外市场。
晶科能源中标100MW组件采购
8月17日，文昌市昌洒镇100MW复合光伏项目光伏组件设备采购中标结果公告发布，晶科能源中标，含税投标总报价约8760.94万元，折合单价约0.73元/W。
项目位于海南省文昌市昌洒镇，规划直流侧容量120MWp、交流侧容量100MW，共建设32个光伏发电单元，包括29个3.2MW单元和3个2.6MW单元。
弘元绿能供货80MW光伏项目
近日，中核镶黄旗40万千瓦风光储一体化基地80MW光伏区组件及设备安装工作全面完成，项目正式进入电气接线与系统调试阶段。弘元绿能为该项目提供高效N型单晶硅双面双玻组件。
据了解，该基地总装机规模400MW，涵盖风电、光伏及储能等业态。其中，80MW光伏区共安装弘元绿能组件13.91万块。
华晟获巴基斯坦HJT组件订单
近日，华晟新能源与Futex集团旗下Air Solution在巴基斯坦拉合尔签署100MW高效HJT组件供货协议。
据悉，这是华晟新能源Himalaya PLUS系列的首个海外订单。目前，该系列产品已实现量产，并完成国内市场交付及欧洲市场首秀。
未来，华晟新能源将支持Air Solution在巴基斯坦三大主要城市设立技术与体验中心，为当地客户提供更完善的售后服务保障。
尚德供货马来西亚工商业光伏
近日，尚德高效光伏组件落地马来西亚莎阿南一处工商业综合体屋顶光伏项目，并完成全流程调试及并网发电。
该项目位于马来西亚雪兰莪州莎阿南市，采用屋顶分布式光伏模式，所发电力主要用于综合体酒店、办公及商业等场景自用。项目采用尚德高效光伏组件，以适应当地气候及工商业屋顶应用场景。

title: 超215亿元，固德威等8企储能/固态电池产能布局加速
content:
近期，多地储能、电池产能建设进一步提速。固德威、陀一固能等企业加快储能及固态电池产能布局，星空集团、中钠储能推进钠离子电池项目，湖南金维则落地全钒液流储能项目。
固德威6GWh储能基地二期项目奠基
8月18日，固德威（广德）新能源产业园二期生产基地项目奠基。该项目重点布局中大型储能系统生产，总投资5.38亿元，规划建设6GWh储能系统产能。
据介绍，固德威广德产业园一期主要布局户用储能，此次二期则聚焦中大型储能赛道。项目建成后，广德基地将形成覆盖户用、工商业及大型储能的产能布局。
300MWh全钒液流储能项目获批
8月17日，湖南金维新材料科技有限公司300MWh全钒液流储能电池装备智能制造基地项目环评获湖南省怀化市生态环境局批复。
项目位于怀化市高新技术产业开发区中方片区（泸阳），总投资2.5亿元，拟租赁现有厂房建设，总建筑面积约3090平方米。项目建成后将形成年产300MWh全钒液流储能电池产能。
星空集团签约南浔钠离子电池智能工厂
8月15日，星空集团与浙江湖州南浔经济开发区签署钠离子电池智能工厂项目协议，具体投资金额及产能规模暂未披露。
据了解，星空集团已在四川达州东部经开区布局了四川星空钠离子电池产业综合项目，项目总投资达115亿元，计划分三阶段建设，主要建设钠离子电芯、PACK集成、钠离子电池储能电站及110kV变电站配电线路、智能电网管理系统等，产品广泛应用于工业商业储能风光发电储能、低速交通备用电源等领域。
陀一固能30GWh固态电池项目开工
8月13日，陀一固能（内蒙古）科技有限责任公司固态电池项目在唿和浩特市土默特左旗开工建设。
该项目总投资60亿元，计划分三期建设，每期投资20亿元、规划产能10GWh，全部建成后将形成30GWh固态电池年产能。其中，一期项目占地约371亩，计划建设电芯厂房、极片生产车间、成品生产线，以及研发中心、仓储物流等配套设施。
先进方形全固态电池项目落地苏州
8月13日，先进方形全固态电池产业化项目在江苏苏州吴中区签约，项目由中国科学院物理研究所与中科低碳城市发展（苏州）有限公司共同推进。
项目首期将建设0.2GWh电芯中试线和4GWh PACK产线，目标两年内实现产品出货，主要面向具身智能、低空经济、电动航空等应用领域。
2.2GWh钠电项目预计9月投产
据正宁发布消息，中钠储能新能源科技（甘肃）有限公司二期石墨烯钠离子电芯项目已进入施工攻坚阶段，预计将于今年9月竣工投产。
据了解，该项目总投资10亿元，于2023年3月开工，分两期实施。其中，一期投资1.8亿元，已建成年产3GWh储能生产线和1GWh锂电池生产线，并实现投产；二期计划投资8.2亿元，建设2.2GWh石墨烯钠离子电芯生产线。
安高特电固态电池项目加快建设
近日，浙江安高特电科技有限公司固态电池总部及研发生产基地项目正在加快建设，一期工程已完成约70%，基建部分预计8月底至9月中旬完工。
项目总投资21.2亿元，计划分三期建设，五年内形成年产3.5GWh固态电池产能。其中，一期投资约2.8亿元，规划建设0.55GWh固态电池产线。
目前，一期一号厂房主体建设正在推进，动力辅房即将封顶，仓库主体结构接近完工，生产车间地基已完成。同时，二号厂房内一条干法层压固态电池小试线已投入运行。
1GWh全固态电池项目将试产
近期，纯锂新能源全固态储能电池项目生产设备已进入安装调试阶段，一期预计9月底试生产。
项目一期总投资1.5亿元，规划建设1GWh全固态电池量产产线，目前大部分设备已完成初步安装，即将开展全线联合调试。
项目一期预计产能可达1GWh至2GWh，产品主要应用于小动力、储能、船舶动力、低空经济、机器人及特种装备等领域。该项目整体分两期建设，全部建成达产后预计形成6GWh全固态电池产能。

title: 阳光电源埃及10GWh储能系统工厂开建
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，据外媒报道，当地时间8月17日，阳光电源位于埃及苏伊士运河经济区TEDA工业开发区的储能系统工厂举办奠基仪式。
该工厂计划总投资5000万美元（约合人民币3.39亿元），厂区占地面积约5万㎡，规划储能系统年产能10GWh，计划2027年4月建成投产。
据悉，这是阳光电源在中东和非洲地区建设的首座储能系统制造基地，也是中东北非区域首个专业储能系统工厂。2026年1月，该项目签署合作及土地相关协议，到8月17日奠基，周期仅七个月，在海外大型新能源制造项目中推进速度较快。
按照规划，该工厂主要完成电池储能系统组装生产。项目锁定埃及本土市场，同时依托苏伊士运河经济区港口物流优势，面向中东、非洲，还可辐射南欧区域。
值得注意的是，该工厂将直接配套挪威新能源企业Scatec在埃及明亚省打造的可持续能源谷（Energy Valley）大型光储项目，为该项目4GWh储能配套提供设备供给。
据悉，埃及工业部长哈立德・哈希姆参与了阳光电源苏伊士工厂的奠基仪式。哈希姆表示，阳光电源储能系统工厂的落地，是埃及搭建本土储能制造基地的重要一步。
对阳光电源而言，埃及工厂是其继欧洲波兰工厂之后，又一处海外实体制造支点。回顾此前，在今年2月，阳光电源宣布欧洲首座制造工厂定址波兰。
阳光电源波兰工厂总投资额约2.3亿欧元（约合人民币18.02亿），占地面积6.54万㎡。新工厂规划年产20GW光伏逆变器及12.5GWh储能系统的制造能力，预计在未来12个月内建成并投入运营。

title: Sunfire starts building SOEC pilot plant at BASF facility

German electrolyser firm Sunfire has started building a 1.3MW solid oxide electrolysis (SOEC) pilot plant at BASF’s Schwarzheide chemical site.
The plant at BASF Infraservice & Solutions’ Industriepark Lausitz aims to validate the company’s latest generation of SOEC technology, which it claims can achieve 89% lower-heating-value electrical efficiency by operating at around 850ºC.
The project comes as Sunfire continues to back SOEC commercialisation despite several major electrolyser manufacturers scaling back their ambitions for the technology.
Sunfire expects the BASF project to be among its final SOEC pilot deployments before moving towards commercial-scale projects.
“Through validation under real industrial conditions, we are completing the final steps before implementing the first commercial projects,” said Sunfire CTO Christian von Olshausen.
Construction has begun
just three months after
the project was announced in May. BASF Infraservice & Solutions Lausitz Chair Jürgen Fuchs attributed the rapid progress to the quick completion of grid-connection testing.
It also follows the start-up of a
2.6MW Sunfire SOEC
system at Neste’s refinery in Rotterdam last October, despite a wider roll-back on SOEC from electrolyser companies.
Earlier this month, compatriot Thyssenkrupp Nucera became the second high-profile firm to put SOEC manufacturing plans on ice, taking a
€30m ($35m) write-down
just over a year after it opened a pilot factory with Fraunhofer IKTS.
In May, Danish technology group Topsoe announced it would
“hibernate”
its EU-funded 500MW SOEC factory, citing weak market demand.
Both companies suggest that, despite the potential of the technology, it was too
nascent to compete
for a market share in the meantime. Currently, there are no large-scale plants operating globally.
However, Sunfire CEO Nils Aldag said that despite its pressurised alkaline systems being rolled out across Europe, the company saw SOEC as “another key technology.”
Aldag previously told members of the press in May that he thought Sunfire’s approach to commercialising SOEC was more “cautious.”
“We’re a bit more cautious, a bit more step by step, and validate the technology before building up significant production capacities, investing hundreds of millions into production sites,” he said.
“We will demonstrate the equipment in 2027 that we’re placing with BASF, and based on that proof of concept, there are then the next scale-up steps planned in our roadmap – say 2030 onwards.”

title: Enapter starts AEM stack production in Shenzhen
content:
The stacks are being produced at Runqing Hydrogen Technology, a subsidiary of the Runshihua Group, on a production line set up specifically for Enapter. The first stacks for Enapter electrolyzers in the megawatt range have already been assembled. Once the current ramp-up phase is complete, Enapter said it expects intended production output to be reached within a few weeks, with capacity scalable in line with demand.
The move is part of an asset-light business model realignment that Enapter announced on 5 August 2026. By shifting stack manufacturing to a partner facility in China, the company is reducing its fixed costs and said it expects the lower fixed cost base to have a noticeable positive effect on earnings development from 2027.
Runqing’s parent, the Runshihua Group, operates fully automated production facilities and has established hydrogen expertise focused on industrial decarbonization.
Dr Jürgen Laakmann, Chief Executive Officer of Enapter AG, said: “The production start in Shenzhen is an important milestone in the implementation of our asset-light business model. Together with our partner Runshihua, we have created the conditions for scalable series production in a short space of time. Thanks to the modern production facilities, we will be able to manufacture the AEM stack, the core component of our electrolysers, cost-efficiently, reliably and in high volumes. This enables us to respond flexibly to rising market demand and to supply our customers quickly and dependably.”

title: Audi’s China-Built EVs Are Coming To Europe—And They Cost Less Than Local Models
content:
Audi’s China-Built EVs Are Coming To Europe—And They Cost Less Than Local Models
Audi went out of its way to keep the Chinese-market E5 and E7X officially out of Europe. A third-party company is importing them anyway.
- Audi developed two new EVs specifically for China.
- The flagship E5 Sportback and E7X SUV were never meant to be sold in Europe.
- Now, though, a company is importing and selling them in Audi’s backyard.
Pretty much everyone knows by now that China’s car market is different from the one in America and Europe. Chinese car buyers want a tech-heavy car that’s also affordable and luxurious, which has forced Western automakers to ditch their traditional offerings and go for a local approach.
It’s why Audi, like others, has set up a separate brand in China and is relying on two EVs built from the ground up for the Chinese market. The company’s all-caps AUDI marque tapped SAIC, its Chinese partner, to make the E5 Sportback and E7X EVs, and they’re quite impressive, sitting on 800- and 900-volt platforms and featuring interiors that look like movie theaters and not ordinary cars.
AUDI E7X (2026)
Audi never intended to sell these EVs in Europe, but an independent company is doing it anyway. Auto China, which has been known to import, homologate, and register Chinese-only cars like the Xiaomi SU7 Ultra and Zeekr 9X, is now doing the same with Audi’s offerings.
Despite the added costs for shipping and homologation, the top-spec Audi E5 and E7X are actually cheaper than their European-made counterparts. For instance, the E5 has a dual-motor, 776-horsepower powertrain and a 100-kilowatt-hour battery, but it’s a whopping €28,000 ($32,500) more affordable than the S6 Sportback e-tron. The sporty European EV is also powered by a 100 kWh battery, but power is down to 543 hp.
A screenshot showing Auto China's website, with the two Chinese AUDI EVs listed for sale.
The same goes for the two electric SUVs. China’s E7X starts from roughly €86,800 ($100,700) shipped and registered in Europe, including VAT. Meanwhile, the smaller, less powerful, and Lidar-less Audi SQ6 e-tron starts from €93,800 ($108,800) in Germany.
The importer includes a charging adapter with each purchase of a Chinese-market EV, and a two-year warranty is also being offered through an independent repair network.
It’s looking like it’s too good to be true, but the first Chinese Audi EVs are already roaming the streets in Germany, according to Automobilwoche. However, buying a Chinese-spec car for European roads might prove a little problematic for owners. First, there’s little know-how regarding the repair processes, and spare parts availability is a huge question mark.
The AUDI E5 Sportback features a pillar-to-pillar interior display. A comprehensive ADAS suite with a Lidar and 11 cameras is also part of the package.
What’s more, the advanced driver assistance systems that use sophisticated sensors were calibrated for China’s roads and might not work as expected in other parts of the world.
„The models of the sister brand AUDI are based on their own platform (Advanced Digitized Platform) developed together with our partner SAIC and are deeply integrated into China's digital ecosystem“, an Audi spokesperson told Automobilwoche.
Then, there’s the issue of longevity. The first cars have already been imported, but if Audi decides to put an end to the whole operation, owners might find themselves struggling to keep their EVs on the road. A few years ago, another dealer imported roughly 20 Chinese-market Volkswagen ID.6 EVs and tried to sell them. Volkswagen sued in 2023 and forced the dealer to freeze sales and ultimately destroy the cars that had already been imported.
„As a dealer, I would not bring vehicles from China,” said Ansgar Klein, president of the Federal Association of Free Motor Vehicle Dealers (BVfK). “Even if the lawyers give the green light, there remains a de facto residual risk.“

title: Kia Niro EV And Hyundai Kona EV Get A 30% Cheaper Motor Replacement
content:
These Affordable EVs Just Got A New Lifeline: Replacement Motors Cost 30% Less
The same company that remanufactures motors for the Tesla Model S now caters to the more affordable Kia Niro and Hyundai Kona EVs
- The first-generation Hyundai Kona and Kia Niro EVs are known for their failing drive units.
- Now, a German company is offering a cheaper alternative to the replacements offered by dealers.
- The same company makes plug-and-play replacements for the first-generation Tesla Model S.
Electric cars are a lot simpler than combustion vehicles, but even simple things can break. And when they do, the bills can be quite high, especially if we’re talking about affordable cars
These first-generation Hyundai Kona and Kia Niro crossovers were some of the most affordable EVs in the United States when they were new, and you could get a good used one for roughly $15,000. They can’t touch today’s EVs in terms of speed, range, or charging performance, but back in the day, they were some of the best out there.
2020 Hyundai Kona Electric
But both suffer from the same problem. One of the reduction gearbox bearings on the front drive unit is known to fail, leading to what enthusiasts and owners have dubbed the “wheel of fortune” ticking. Replacing the transmission at the dealer can cost anywhere from $2,500 to $5,000, which is a third of the car’s entire value.
Now, though, a German company claims it can help owners save up to 30% while also getting replacement parts that are as good as new.
SEG Automotive, known for making starters and alternators, is now also remanufacturing drive units for electric cars. The company started with the Large Drive Unit (LDU) fitted to the first-generation Tesla Model S, and then added the Renault Zoe to its portfolio. From the end of this year, SEG will also offer remanufactured drive units for the Kia Niro EV and Hyundai Niro EV under its Redrive brand.
SEG Automotive remanufactured Tesla Model S Large Drive Unit
The German company said it’s refurbishing everything, including the electric motor, transmission, and inverter. New bearings and seals are installed, and known vulnerabilities are addressed. In the case of the Tesla LDU, which is known to leak coolant, SEG installs a coolant delete to keep old drive units on the road for longer.
For the first-gen Kia Niro EV and Hyundai Kona EV, the Redrive units will be available for both the 134- and 201-horsepower versions. To get a remanufactured SEG drive unit, owners should get in touch with an authorized repair shop, which can send the faulty unit to SEG to get it refurbished.
The newly introduced Kia Niro and Hyundai Kona remanufactured drive units will be unveiled next month at the Automechanika show in Frankfurt, which runs from 8 to 12 September.

title: LG Energy Solution's Newest Battery Megafactory Just Kicked Off Production
content:
LG Energy Solution's Newest Battery Megafactory Just Kicked Off Production
This Lansing, Michigan plant will employ up to 1,700 people and produce up to 35 GWh worth of batteries per year.
- This plant will produce battery cells for both cars and energy storage systems.
- The Toyota Highlander will use NMC cells from this plant. The energy storage systems will use LFP cells.
- This facility will employ up to 1,700 people and produce up to 35 GWh worth of cells per year.
LG Energy Solution announced today that it has officially started production of EV batteries in its new facility in Lansing, Michigan. This 226-acre plant will be instrumental in providing EV battery cells and modules to key products from some well-known car brands.
The 226-acre facility has had more than $2 billion of investment, and currently employs 900 people. At maximum capacity, this facility will employ 1,700 people and produce up to 35 GWh of production per year.
LGES says that this factory will serve a pivotal role in Michigan’s manufacturing capabilities, producing cells and large-scale battery storage solutions for different brands.
One of the most notable clients for this factory is Toyota. LG will produce nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) lithium battery modules for the upcoming all-electric three-row Toyota Highlander. These cells will travel to the Georgetown, Kentucky plant, which shows a big investment in America’s EV supply chain. A major part of the Highlander’s supply chain will stay here in the country.
But the facility doesn't just produce NMC cells and packs. LG will also build lower-cost lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) cells for energy storage systems, with Tesla as a key customer.
This is great news for EV production and for manufacturing jobs. LGES plans to have 50 GWh of battery production capacity all over North America. This includes not just the Lansing plant but also LG’s other plants in Holland, Michigan, Nextar Energy plant in Windsor, Ontario and an upcoming facility in Arizona among its North American footprint. The figure also includes joint-venture plants, like the Ultium cell plant in Tennessee, and LG's partnership with Honda in Ohio.
Luckily, it seems like the Lansing plant is fairly future-proofed. Whereas slower-than-expected sales of the Ultium platform cars and the cancellation of Honda’s EV platform have no doubt been a damper on LG’s joint venture plants, the ability to focus on energy storage solutions has been a saving grace. Also, Toyota has been remarkably committed as of late to full electrification. The new Highlander EV is one of the seven fully electric models planned to be launched by 2027. If they’re American-made, then I wouldn’t be surprised if LG Energy Solution’s plant ends up making more than just batteries for the new Highlander.

title: This 100-Year-Old EV Came With More Range Than The First Nissan Leaf
content:
This 100-Year-Old EV Came With More Range Than The First Nissan Leaf
There's a catch, though. You better be cool with going slow.
I'm not trying to pick on the O.G. Nissan Leaf. It was a groundbreaking car that brought electrification to the masses before anything else. But it wasn't exactly a long-range EV. In fact, it offered a similar range to this nearly 100-year-old EV. According to Mecum Auctions, this 1918 Detroit Electric Model 75B, that went up for auction during Monterey Car Week, had an original range of 80 miles. There are Mk7 VW e-Golfs that'd be happy with that range. It does come with a caveat, though: the Detroit Electric had a top speed of just 20 mph, so you can assume that it wasn't exactly tested on the EPA range cycle.
Built by the Anderson Electric Car Company, the Detroit Electric had 42 separate lead-acid batteries, 21 at the front and 21 at the rear. They powered a single 4.28-horsepower electric motor mounted under the floor that sent power to a rear differential. This specific example is a bit different, though, because it's been fitted with modern batteries. There's no word on what its range is with the newer batteries, but I'd imagine it's quite a bit more.
It's pretty odd inside, though. There's seating for four, with a bench seat on one side and two individual seats across from it. However, it looks like the driver sits on the left side of the bench, with a steering tiller, two pedals in front of them, and one at the base of their seat, as if it's operated by the driver's heel. It also looks like someone can sit directly in the driver's line of sight, which probably isn't the best. It looks cozy, though, with cushy fabric seats, curtains for the rear windows, and a big greenhouse with lots of tall glass.
Sure, it can only do 20 mph, which is too slow for even most low-speed vehicle rules in the United States, but I bet it's a blast to drive. Instant electric torque in something that old must be fun, even if it tops out quickly. It also looks spectacularly vintage. The black and burgundy two-tone color scheme looks lovely and those old school wire wheels are fantastically old-school. There are some modern bicycles with wider wheels and tires than this thing has. It's just such a cool vibe.
This thing must have been mind-blowing back in its day. Smooth, quiet motoring without the smells of pre-catalytic converter engines, and no difficult cranking? Now, it's probably the easiest classic car to drive from that era for all of those same reasons. Although, it might be wise for its next owner to swap out its motor for one that can give it a top speed of at least residential speeds.

China's Apple Car has been a major success.
In just 28 months, tech company Xiaomi managed to sell more than a half-million examples of its first EV.
It's sold a total of 760,000 EVs since April 2024.
It seems like just yesterday that the Xiaomi name was unknown in the car world. The company was known as a consumer technology brand. But it was a full 28 months ago that the company dove headfirst into the auto industry. It suddenly introduced its first ever EV: the
And boy, was it a hit. Now, just over two years into producing cars, Xiaomi has sold more than 500,000 SU7s. The company's nascent electric car division is quickly turning into an automotive empire.

title: Win11 旧版 Media Player 再遭削弱：微软引导用户使用内存占用更高的新版应用
content:
8 月 19 日消息，据 Windows Latest 今日报道，微软正逐步削弱 Windows 经典媒体播放器 Windows Media Player 的功能。
Windows 观察人士 Xeno Panther 发现，在
最新实验版中，旧版播放器的字幕控制选项已被阉割，用户尝试启用字幕时会被提示转向新版播放器。
Windows 11
Experimental（Future Platforms）Build 29648.1000 中。
在旧版媒体播放器中，如果你右击正在播放的内容，并将鼠标悬停在“歌词、字幕”和“副标题”上，则会出现三个选项“关闭”、“可用时打开”和“默认设置”，如今仅剩“可用时打开”。
进一步尝试开启字幕后，播放器会弹出提示，称无法在 Windows Media Player 中启用字幕，并要求用户转向新版 Windows Media Player。
微软目前没有将这一变化列入正式的 Media Player 更新说明，因此现阶段更适合视为实验性版本中的功能调整。
同时，Windows Insider 的 Experimental（Future Platforms）版本本身也属于早期测试版本，其中部分功能可能最终不会进入正式版。
微软实际上已经在新版 Media Player 中持续完善字幕功能。2026 年 6 月发布的 Media Player 11.2605.14.0 更新增加了自定义字幕功能，用户可以根据 Windows 的字幕设置调整字幕样式，同时能够直接从播放器进入相关系统设置。
目前 Win11 仍可保留旧版 Windows Media Player，但微软将其定位为可选功能，并针对现代视频功能推荐使用新版 Media Player。
微软官方支持页面显示，Windows 11 用户仍可通过“可选功能”安装 Windows Media Player，而对于 4K 等现代视频功能，微软推荐使用新版 Media Player。
不过，新版播放器与旧版播放器之间仍存在一定差异。测试显示，旧版播放器启动视频的速度更快。此外，新版 Media Player 空闲状态下占用约 377 MB 内存，而旧版播放器仅为 103.4 MB，前者约为后者的 3.6 倍。
另外，编解码器支持也是两者之间的主要区别之一。旧版 Media Player 可以直接播放 HEVC 视频，而新版 Media Player 还需要额外购买并安装 HEVC 视频拓展插件（或离线安装）。微软官方文档也说明，当媒体文件需要用户未安装的编解码器时，Media Player 会显示相应提示。
IT之家注意到，旧版 Media Player 还保留了传统媒体库以及音频 CD 刻录等功能。与此同时，微软已经逐步减少对旧版播放器的维护，此前其用于向兼容设备同步音乐的“Sync”选项也已经消失。

title: 《漫威斗魂》PC 版发售 11 天即遭破解，玩家称破解版明显更流畅
content:
8 月 19 日消息，4v4 团队格斗游戏《漫威斗魂》自 8 月 6 日登陆 PS5 与 PC 平台后就一直受到玩家诟病，尤其是 PC 版强制绑定 PSN 账号和游戏优化问题。
据 Wccftech 等多家媒体报道，《漫威斗魂》在发售仅 11 天后即遭破解，更令开发商 Arc System Works 及发行商索尼陷入尴尬的是 —— 据玩家反映，破解后的无 DRM 版本运行起来显著比官方版流畅。
《漫威斗魂》发售初期曾迅速登顶 Steam 畅销榜，但用户评价旋即跌至“褒贬不一”。截至 8 月 19 日，Steam 平台约 3500 至 4200 条用户评测中，好评率仅 47%。
尽管游戏媒体评分尚可（IGN 及 GameSpot 均给出 9 分），但玩家反馈并没有想象中那么好，问题多集中在帧率波动、持续微卡顿、游戏崩溃、画面设置异常及网络代码问题（含回滚机制异常），即便在远超推荐配置的硬件上亦未能幸免。
引发玩家强烈不满的另一点在于，PC 版强制要求绑定 PSN 账号方可进行在线对战，这也导致全球超 130 个国家及地区的玩家无法购买或游玩游戏 —— 尽管故事模式与街机模式等离线内容无需 PSN 账号。
此外，Steam Deck 与 Linux 用户因反作弊机制完全无法启动游戏。PS5 版则基本规避了上述问题，因此有玩家推测，PC 版性能劣化或源于 DRM 及反作弊软件所带来的性能开销。
据盗版追踪网站 CrackWatch 记录，《漫威斗魂》于当地时间 8 月 17 日被破解小组成功绕过 DRM 保护。随后，玩过破解版的玩家在 Reddit、ResetEra 等平台反馈称，其性能表现远超正版。
一位 Reddit 用户称，其使用破解版在最高画质设定下可稳定运行 60 帧，且无需如正版般预热着色器才能获得较稳定的表现；另一位用户 JustinSGX 则表示，破解版在其 i7-6700K 处理器上的占用率仅约 34%，而正版游戏 CPU 占用率高达 57%。还有玩家称，破解版中等画质可稳定 60 帧，CPU / GPU 占用率约 40-50%，而正版“即便在 GBA 分辨率下也卡在 45 帧”。
多数人认为，造成性能差异的主因是正版同时运行了反作弊系统（Easy Anti-Cheat）及 PSN 相关后台进程。移除 DRM 的同时也移除了这些额外负载。Arc System Works 已公开承认性能问题，表示“团队正积极调查相关报告”，但截至IT之家发稿仍未提供进一步的说明。
实际上，移除 DRM 后游戏性能大增的案例很常见，但此次《漫威斗魂》DRM 在不到两周内即遭破解，未能有效阻止盗版，反而给正版付费玩家带来了负面体验，成为 DRM 适得其反的典型案例。

title: 中国科大领衔团队首次利用“暗腔”实现超导无接触增强，成果登上《自然》
content:
IT之家 8 月 19 日消息，中国科学技术大学曾长淦教授、程广珲教授领衔的研究团队，联合上海交通大学蒋庆东副教授、麻省理工学院弗兰克 · 维尔切克教授等合作者，在量子物态调控领域取得重要进展。
研究团队首次利用“暗腔”实现了真空涨落对超导的增强效应。相关成果于 8 月 19 日发表于《自然》。
在量子电动力学中，真空并非真正的“空无一物”，而是伴随着虚粒子的不断产生与湮灭，如同充满量子涨落的动态“海洋”。然而，自由空间中的真空涨落通常较弱，难以对宏观凝聚态体系产生可观测影响。如何将其转化为调控量子物态的资源，是凝聚态物理与腔量子电动力学交叉领域的重要课题。
为此，曾长淦、程广珲团队引入了由太赫兹分裂环谐振器构成的“暗腔”。“暗腔”是一种不含外部光子的电磁谐振结构，通过重塑局域电磁环境，可显著增强特定频率的真空涨落。
研究团队将超导体二硒化铌（NbSe₂）嵌入暗腔，发现其超导临界温度获得实质性提高 —— 在六层二硒化铌器件中，临界温度最高提升了 5.4%。
同时，超导体的临界电流和临界磁场在超导转变附近也显著增强。这是国际上首次通过实验观测到真空涨落对超导的增强效应。
通过严格的对照实验，团队排除了应变、退化、非均匀性等常规因素的干扰。实验发现，超导增强效应随暗腔特征频率呈现共振峰形依赖关系，这为超导态与暗腔的耦合提供了关键证据。
在理论层面，蒋庆东研究组与弗兰克 · 维尔切克提出：超导态通过与暗腔交换虚光子，降低了自身能量，从而增强了超导性。当腔模的特征能量与超导材料的低能涨落能量相匹配时，超导增强效应最强。
该研究通过腔体工程化调控真空涨落，实现了对超导稳态的无外部驱动、非接触式增强。这一全新的“非接触式旋钮”为探索超导机理与设计新型超导器件提供了新思路，有望在量子物态调控领域获得广泛应用。

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11037-x。

。其中最关键的部分是 Seed Foundation Model （Seed 基础模型）成立了四个新的一级部门：

，提升模型的基础智能上限。

Agentic 模型的整合与发布
，并针对办公场景优化模型的 Agentic 能力，包括支持豆包和 Dola 的任务模式。

四个新部门的负责人均向吴永辉汇报。此外，Seed 还为 AI 安全及其他前沿探索方向分别任命了负责人。Seed 在这次调整公告中提到：“合并相似工作、减少 overlap（重合），内聚在一起”。
在此之前，Seed 主要按照
划分团队，文本、代码、视觉、推理等方向都有自己的数据、后训练团队。这一机制在大模型研发早期利于快速补齐不同能力，但团队间的边界随着研究方向增多而变得越来越模糊，导致出现了“重复造轮子”的情形，提高了跨团队沟通和协作的成本。
据IT之家了解，本月早些时候，该媒体发布了字节跳动正在讨论训练
参数规模超 5 万亿模型
的消息。该模型将超过阿里的 Qwen 3.8-Max（2.4 万亿参数）和月之暗面的 K3（2.8 万亿参数），也是目前
国内已知参数规模最大
的模型。通常而言，模型规模越大，智能水平往往越高，不过该计划仍处于早期阶段。
而这一计划，也给了字节跳动打破
原有团队边界和分工模式
的更强决心和动力。调整中的一个明显变化，就是将负责应用后训练的团队按照用户任务
拆分为 Work 和 Chat 两个方向

title: 原价 19.99 美元 / 月的 AI 助手免费送，亚马逊 Alexa+ 登陆全美所有受支持的 Fire TV
content:
IT之家 8 月 19 日消息，当地时间 19 日（今天），亚马逊宣布将向美国所有兼容的 Fire TV 设备免费提供 Alexa+，不论用户是否订阅 Amazon Prime。升级后，Fire TV 将获得对话式搜索、智能家居控制和 AI 推荐等功能。
此前，未订阅 Amazon Prime 的用户使用 Alexa+ 需要每月支付 19.99 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 135.1 元人民币），而且这项服务最初只向亚马逊去年秋季发布的新款 Fire TV 设备开放。
亚马逊表示，兼容设备会自动升级到 Alexa+，用户不需要额外下载应用，也不用单独订阅。支持范围包括所有现款 Amazon Fire TV Stick、Fire TV Cube、亚马逊 Ember 智能电视，以及海信和松下等内置 Alexa+ 的智能电视。
亚马逊的做法延续了消费电子行业扩大 AI 覆盖范围的趋势，这类升级往往会直接推送给用户。谷歌今年早些时候把 Gemini 带到了 Google TV 平台，以 AI 对话模式取代原本较为简单的搜索功能；Roku 去年也为语音助理加入了 AI 能力。
厂商通常会用功能使用时长等数据来证明消费者正在接受这些 AI 服务。亚马逊表示，Alexa+ 用户目前在 Fire TV 上的对话次数接近使用原版 Alexa 时的两倍。按照亚马逊的解读，用户已经不再只是把电视当作单纯观看内容的设备，也开始主动使用电视上的 AI 功能。
Alexa+ 不再要求用户必须说出具体片名。用户可以直接按照题材、适合年龄或热门程度提出要求，例如“推荐一部评分很高的惊悚片”，或者“一部以强势女性为主角的历史剧”。
此外，Alexa+ 还可以用来管理和控制智能家居设备，例如在电视上直接显示 Ring 摄像头的实时画面。

title: 嫦娥七号发射在即：将赴充满未知的月球南极，首要任务寻找水冰
content:
IT之家 8 月 19 日消息，今日，嫦娥七号探测器和长征五号遥十四运载火箭在中国文昌航天发射场完成技术区相关工作，器箭组合体已垂直转运至发射区，计划近日择机实施发射。
据央视财经报道，嫦娥七号即将奔赴充满未知的月球南极，执行极具挑战性的综合探测任务。
工程层面，嫦娥七号将突破多项关键技术：高精度月面软着陆、月面腿式行走、月面飞跃、永久阴影坑原位探测等等。
月球南极分布大量永久阴影坑，坑内常年不见阳光，极低温环境下，有可能保存数十亿年的水冰资源，这是未来月球驻留的宝贵资源，也是本次探测的重中之重。
嫦娥七号的科学目标清晰明确：探测月表环境、月壤水冰与挥发组分；开展月球南极形貌、物质成分、地质构造高精度探测；探测月壳浅层结构、月震、磁场、热特性、空间环境；开展月基天文观测，同时搭载多国合作载荷，推进月球探测国际合作。
嫦娥七号获取的南极第一手数据，将为嫦娥八号建设国际月球科研站基本型，提供关键科学支撑，助力人类揭开月球南极的重重谜题。
IT之家注：嫦娥七号目标直指月球南纬 85 度以上的南极-艾特肯盆地，中国有望成为全球首个在月球找到水的国家。

content:
8 月 19 日消息，据 NeoWin 今日报道，微软近年来频繁调整产品名称，如今甚至有粉丝专门为此搭建了一个网站，用于记录微软现有产品的改名历史。
https://www.msrebrandregistry.com/
）已经收录 72 款微软产品及其历史上的 158 个曾用名，并通过数据图表统计微软不同年份的改名情况。
这一网站名为“Rebrand Registry”，由微软 MVP（Most Valuable Professional）Loryan Strant 创建，主要记录目前仍在运营、但历史上曾经更改过名称的微软产品。
Strant 此前还创建过“Let Me Correct That For You”网站，专门纠正微软产品名称的大小写不一致问题，例如 OneDrive 采用驼峰式大小写命名，而 Copilot 则使用常规大写命名。
网站数据显示，微软产品的名称平均存活时间为两年零十一个月。有 8 款产品经历过三次更名，包括 Azure AI 搜索、Azure 应用服务、Azure DevOps、Azure SQL 数据库、Foundry Tools、Microsoft 365 Copilot 应用、Microsoft Configuration Manager 和 Microsoft Defender for Endpoint。
该网站还设有“更名风险指数”，试图预测微软下一款会改名的产品。该预测基于当前名称已使用时长、曾用名数量以及该产品系列历史上的更名频率等因素。因此，Azure 应用服务、Azure SQL 数据库、Azure DevOps 和 Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service 更名可能性被标记为“较高”。
Strant 在接受 The Register 采访时表示，他认为这个网站是一个有用的资源，同时也希望它能让访问者“会心一笑”。
IT之家注意到，该网站还提供了微软产品改名趋势统计。数据显示，从 2012 年至今，2023 年是微软产品改名最频繁的一年，当年共有 18 款产品改过名。

title: 最看好 AI 的人成了最怀疑 AI 的人，美国 30 岁以下成年人担心技术进步引发失业潮
content:
8 月 19 日消息，据彭博社今天（19 日）报道，皮尤研究中心调查显示，美国最年轻的一批劳动者对 AI 的怀疑态度正愈发增强，他们越来越担心技术进步会
造成大规模岗位流失
自皮尤 2021 年开始进行这项调查以来，
的 30 岁以下成年人对 AI 的担忧开始多于期待。最年轻群体的转变尤其显著：过去最看好 AI 的发展潜力的一群人，现在却已经成为对 AI 最怀疑的人群之一。这一年龄段
近四分之三的成年人
还认为，AI 会减少就业机会，比例高于两年前的 61%。
此外，其他大多数年龄群体也持类似态度。
这样的结果进一步体现了美国年轻人与 AI 之间的矛盾关系。他们既是最熟练使用 AI 的人群之一，又恰好在这项技术可能削弱初级岗位之际进入职场，而初级岗位长期以来一直是年轻人进入就业市场的重要入口。
这种担忧并不限于年轻人。皮尤数据显示，
超过一半美国人对 AI 感到担忧
。已经在职场站稳脚跟的人对 AI 的态度反而越来越积极，也进一步支持了一种观点：经验越丰富的劳动者，越可能从 AI 中获益。
AI 究竟对美国招聘造成了多大影响，目前仍很难准确判断。AI 快速普及恰逢经济走弱，两种因素难以完全分开。此外，AI 也可能只取代一份工作中的部分任务，而不是整个岗位。
IT之家从报道中获悉，已有迹象显示，面向职场新人的招聘正在放缓，美国企业高管也公开谈到，通过 AI 自动完成部分工作可以降低用工成本。

title: 消息称鸿蒙智行问界儿童车售价达五位数，预计定价 15800 元
content:
IT之家 8 月 19 日消息，鸿蒙智行问界汽车官方此前宣布，问界儿童车即将上市。据介绍，这款新车主打“成长陪伴，智趣探索”，将延续家族经典外观。
博主 @未来的学习笔记 今日分享了一张朋友圈截图，来自问界的销售人员宣布这款儿童车已经可以开启预订，售价为 15800 元。
不过博主表示，问界儿童车的价格可能不准，但五位数应该是错不了的。
IT之家注意到，问界儿童车外观与问界旗舰车型 —— 问界 M9 极为相似，有网友将其戏称为问界“M0.9”。该车采用双座布局设计，配有标志性的大饼轮毂，同时前挡风玻璃上方还有一枚“激光雷达”（放大图片来看，这个部件内嵌的是一枚摄像头）。
预热海报显示，问界儿童车由赛力斯汽车、华为联合设计。

title: 硅谷掀起“晒表”潮：科技公司定制款帝舵腕表成职场身份新象征
content:
IT之家 8 月 19 日消息，据《商业内幕》今天（19 日）报道，一些硅谷从业者开始把职业身份“戴”在手腕上，相比在领英展示履历，他们更愿意晒出由瑞士帝舵为所在公司定制的稀有腕表。
这波晒表热潮始于本周一。一篇展示谷歌员工定制腕表的帖子在网上流传后，其他科技公司员工也陆续晒出了自己的定制表款。
OpenAI 应用研究负责人鲍里斯 · 鲍尔晒出了 OpenAI 定制款，表背刻有“好研究需要时间”。
Palantir 战略合作负责人埃利亚诺 · 尤尼斯也展示了公司员工获得的定制帝舵腕表，并透露该款限量 468 枚。从尤尼斯分享的图片来看，表盘只有一个尺寸很小、十分低调的 Palantir logo。
曾在 Instagram 任职、目前效力于 Perplexity 的塞巴斯蒂安 · 施派尔也分享了自己的定制腕表。曾在 Facebook 工作 6 年的内特 · 洛伦岑说，公司员工当时同样定制过腕表，“我真蠢，居然没有把这些全买下来”。
这些帝舵腕表并不是公司管理层批量发放的普通纪念品，也不同于华尔街一度流行的巴塔哥尼亚马甲。真正发起定制的通常是员工自己组织的腕表收藏团体。成员需要先召集足够多的买家，达到帝舵规定的最低订购数量后才能下单。
根据奢侈腕表新闻网站 Grey Market 执行编辑 Powerfunk 介绍，帝舵定制腕表至少需要订购 40 枚，从下单到完成生产大约需要 6 个月。参加定制的买家通常需要按零售价付款。谷歌定制款采用的帝舵领潜型，普通版本零售价约为 4,500 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 30,406 元人民币）。
由于每款定制腕表数量都很少，而且通常只有发起定制的团体成员才有资格购买，一旦流入二手市场，就可能变成价值不菲的收藏品。
一枚采用 Chrome 恐龙图案的谷歌主题帝舵腕表今年早些时候在拍卖中卖出超过 1 万美元（现汇率约合 67,569 元人民币），苹果“海盗”定制款也曾获得 13,500 美元（现汇率约合 91,218 元人民币）的报价。
同系列普通腕表的二手价格通常只有这些定制版本的一小部分。目前，奢华腕表也越来越成为科技行业大人物展示身份的标志。马克 · 扎克伯格收藏了价值数百万美元的稀有腕表，OpenAI CEO 萨姆 · 奥尔特曼则曾佩戴一枚售价 48 万美元（现汇率约合 324.3 万元人民币）的超限量版高珀富斯腕表，该款全球仅生产 33 枚。

title: 索尼平价降噪耳机 WH-1000XM4C 更多信息曝光：砍掉 NFC、续航略降，保留 QN1 芯片与 40mm 动圈单元
content:
8 月 19 日消息，据 Winfuture 今日报道，索尼即将推出 WH-1000XM4C 头戴式降噪耳机。
作为经典 WH-1000XM4 的衍生版本，这款产品在延续原有外观设计的同时，将蓝牙协议升级至 6.0 版本，同时续航表现略有下滑，预计以更低的价格进入市场。
根据目前曝光的索尼产品资料，WH-1000XM4C 将继续采用 40mm 动圈单元，并支持蓝牙 6.0。新款耳机同样支持主动降噪功能，不过目前尚未公布具体降噪性能指标。
在音频规格方面，WH-1000XM4C 的频率响应范围为 4Hz 至 40000Hz，与上一代产品基本一致。耳机重量约 253 克，与 WH-1000XM4 相同。
从目前曝光的官方图来看，WH-1000XM4C 基本延续了 WH-1000XM4 的整体设计。两款产品在结构和按键布局等方面看起来较为接近，新款主要通过配色进行区分。不过，其左侧耳罩上原有的 NFC 标识已经消失，这意味着索尼可能取消了 NFC 功能。
续航方面，WH-1000XM4C 相比原版有所缩减。曝光资料显示，新款耳机开启主动降噪时最长续航约 27 小时，关闭主动降噪后最长续航约 34 小时。
作为对比，WH-1000XM4 开启主动降噪时最长续航约 30 小时，关闭主动降噪后最长续航约 38 小时。也就是说，WH-1000XM4C 的两种使用模式续航分别减少约 3 小时和 4 小时。
价格方面，此前 @billbil_kun 爆料信息显示，索尼可能为 WH-1000XM4C 设定约 250 欧元
（现汇率约合 1,954 元人民币）
的建议零售价。作为参考，WH-1000XM4 最初在欧洲市场的官方建议零售价为 379 欧元。

title: 红魔游戏平板 5 PRO「氘锋透明银翼」本月 21 日开售，产品总经理称产能限制只能先满足一部分
content:
IT之家 8 月 19 日消息，红魔官方今日宣布，红魔游戏平板 5 PRO 的「氘锋透明银翼」款定档 8 月 21 日 10:10 开售，送 1 年延保 +1 年碎屏保、支持 6 期免息、以旧换新至高补贴 1100 元。
该机已于 6 月 30 日正式发布，采用透明水冷设计，号称“口袋里的游戏神器”，首销 4999 元起、国补价 4499 元起。
红魔游戏手机产品总经理姜超今日发文称，虽然黑色还没能满足大家需求，但很多朋友留言要银色，所以还是安排了些银色生产。他表示，产能限制，也只能先满足一部分了。
据介绍，红魔游戏平板 5 PRO 搭载第五代骁龙 8 至尊版处理器 + 红芯 R4，匹配 ICE 魔冷散热架构。平板内置 8300mAh 电池，搭载双 USB-C 接口，支持 80W 有线充电，支持旁路充电 PRO。
该平板还搭载全新 PC 模拟器 Steam 直连模式，低门槛畅玩 PC 大作。同时内置了 AI 战术教练和 AI 魔姬嘴替两大功能，前者支持赛前赛中提供选英雄、出装战术等游戏指导，后者支持 DeepSeek 自然回复交流，让对手“破防”。
